    of Vasudeva .
    Thus the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the Supersoul of all living entities and who vanquishes all the fear of His devotees, entered the mind of Vasudeva in full opulence.
    Purport

    The word viśvātmā refers to one who is situated in everyone’s heart ( īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṁ hṛd-deśe ’rjuna tiṣṭhati ). Another meaning of viśvātmā is “the only lovable object for everyone.” Because of forgetfulness of this object, people are suffering in this material world, but if one fortunately revives his old consciousness of loving Kṛṣṇa and connects with Viśvātmā, one becomes perfect. The Lord is described in the Third Canto (3.2.15) as follows: parāvareśo mahad-aṁśa-yukto hy ajo ’pi jāto bhagavān. Although unborn, the Lord, the master of everything, appears like a born child by entering the mind of a devotee. The Lord is already there within the mind, and consequently it is not astonishing for Him to appear as if born from a devotee’s body. The word āviveśa signifies that the Lord appeared within the mind of Vasudeva. There was no need for a discharge of semen. That is the opinion of Śrīpāda Śrīdhara Svāmī and Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura. In the Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī, Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī says that consciousness was awakened within the mind of Vasudeva. Śrīla Vīrarāghava Ācārya also says that Vasudeva was one of the demigods and that within his mind the Supreme Personality of Godhead appeared as an awakening of consciousness.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Thus the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the Supersoul of all living entities and who vanquishes all the fear of His devotees, entered the mind of Vasudeva in full opulence.
    Commentary

    Krsna, visvatma, soul of the universe, the object of prema for the whole universe, entered the mind of Vasudeva, along with all his avatara forms (amsa) and his six opulences (bhaga). Amsa here indicates all the avataras such as purusavataras. Bhaga refers to the six opulences or all good qualities. In the third canto it is said: paravareso mahad amsa yukto hy ajo’pi jata bhagavan. The unlimited Lord along with his amsas, though unborn, took his birth.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Though the Lord is the soul of the universe, he appeared in the heart of Vasudeva with special bhāva, since he gives fearlessness to the devotees, complete with all his qualities and powers (bhagavān). Some like Citsukha connect mana with pauruṣaṁ dhāma in the next line.

    Related values & verses
    Related values
    Shraddha (Faith / Reverence)Daksya (Resourcefulness / Skill)Adambhitva (Non-hypocrisy / Authenticity)Dhairya (Composure / Courage)Discriminative Wisdom
    Related verses
    SB 10.2.13 SB 10.2.14 SB 10.2.15 SB 10.2.17 SB 10.2.18 SB 10.2.19 BG 9.11 BG 15.2 BG 6.47 BG 5.4 BG 9.1 BG 4.8
    Concepts
    Jiva
    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa, the Viśvātmā already seated in every heart, awakens within a surrendered devotee's mind and personally drives out all fear.
    Practical Applications
    • Begin the day by remembering that Kṛṣṇa is already present in your heart as Viśvātmā — speak to Him there before you speak to anyone else.
    • Name one fear you have been carrying and explicitly hand it to Kṛṣṇa as bhaktānām abhayaṅkaraḥ, refusing to rehearse it again today.
    • Prepare your mind as Vasudeva's mind was prepared — sit for ten silent minutes in sattva, withdrawing from viṣaya, so the Lord has clean ground to appear within.
    Reflection Questions
    • Vasudeva became a fit vessel because his consciousness was purified — where in my own mind is Kṛṣṇa being crowded out by viṣaya, and what concretely would I have to clear so that He could 'enter' there?
    • If Kṛṣṇa as viśvātmā is already 'the only lovable object' seated in my heart, which lesser objects am I currently treating as more lovable, and what does that misplaced affection cost me each day?
    For Each Age Group
    youth
    • Before opening your phone in the morning, take 60 seconds and remember that Kṛṣṇa is already viśvātmā — already inside the chest you are about to fill with notifications. Notice which 'lovable objects' (a crush, a follower count, a grade) are competing for that seat today.
    • When exam fear or social-rejection fear spikes this week, test the abhayaṅkaraḥ claim directly: chant or pray for two minutes and observe whether the fear's grip loosens. Don't pretend it worked if it didn't — bring honest data back to your sādhana.
    • Pick one peer-pressure decision you're facing (a party, a relationship line, an academic shortcut) and ask: would I make this choice if I genuinely believed Kṛṣṇa is sitting in my heart watching, not as a judge but as the only one whose love actually lasts past graduation?
    householder
    • Tonight, look at your spouse and your children and practice seeing viśvātmā — the same Kṛṣṇa seated in each of their hearts. Let that re-frame one specific irritation or grievance you've been nursing this week.
    • In the next big family financial decision (school, house, job change), formally pause and ask the Lord seated in your heart for guidance before consulting spreadsheets. Test the purport's claim that connection with Viśvātmā perfects ordinary action.
    • Your children are watching where you place your fear. This week, name out loud one anxiety (money, career, health) and explicitly hand it to Kṛṣṇa as bhaktānām abhayaṅkaraḥ in front of them — not as performance, but as instruction by example.
    senior
    • Vasudeva received Kṛṣṇa into his mind in his maturity, not his youth. Spend ten minutes daily clearing the mind of the day's residue so that, like Vasudeva's, it becomes a fit chamber for the Lord to manifest — this is your sādhana now, not productivity.
    • Identify one attachment (a possession, a role, a grudge, a status) that you have carried for decades and that no longer serves the soul's journey. Begin loosening it this month — not by force, but by re-routing that love toward Viśvātmā, the only object that does not decay.
    • When you mentor a younger person — child, grandchild, student — speak less about your achievements and more about the abhaya you have found (or failed to find) in Kṛṣṇa. Mortality is approaching; your real legacy is whether they saw a fearless devotee, not a successful person.
    Common Pitfalls
    • Drifting into impersonalism — hearing 'Supersoul in everyone's heart' and quietly substituting 'the Self within' or 'divine consciousness' for the personal Kṛṣṇa whom Vasudeva actually received.
    • Treating abhayaṅkaraḥ ('vanquisher of the devotee's fear') as a generic anxiety-relief technique — using japa or remembrance as a calming tool for material fears rather than as surrender to the Person who removes the root fear of saṁsāra.
    • Romanticizing 'Kṛṣṇa enters the mind' as a mystical experience to chase, instead of doing the unglamorous sādhana of purifying the mind — sattva, hearing, chanting — that made Vasudeva's mind a fit place for Him to appear.
    Discussion Prompts
    • The purport says Vasudeva conceived Kṛṣṇa without a discharge of semen — Kṛṣṇa simply 'entered his mind.' Take a position with your partner: is this a literal biological claim, a theological metaphor, or both? Defend your reading and locate where the disagreement actually lies.
    • Viśvātmā is glossed as 'the only lovable object for everyone.' Name one person, thing, or pursuit you currently love that you would resist re-routing toward Kṛṣṇa, and say honestly why. Push back on each other — don't let easy renunciations stand.
    • Vasudeva is described as a fit vessel because Kṛṣṇa 'vanquishes all fear of His devotees.' What does it mean that abhaya — fearlessness — is the precondition for Kṛṣṇa to manifest in the mind? Is your sādhana actually producing less fear, or just more managed anxiety? Be specific.
    Role Play

    Two students pair up. Student A is a longtime devotee who has just told a skeptical relative (Student B) that 'Vasudeva conceived Kṛṣṇa in his mind, not through normal conception.' Student B — a thoughtful science-trained cousin at a family dinner — responds with genuine curiosity and pushback: 'So you believe a child literally appeared from a thought? Or is this poetry?' Student A must explain the āviveśa teaching using only what the verse and purport actually say (citing Śrīdhara Svāmī, Viśvanātha Cakravartī, Sanātana Gosvāmī as the purport does), without retreating into 'it's just symbolic' and without sounding defensive. After 7 minutes, swap roles. Debrief: where did A's words feel hollow, and where did they ring true?

    Objections & Responses
    • This is mythological embellishment — a god 'entering a mind' to bypass biology is just pre-scientific people explaining a normal pregnancy with a divine gloss. Why should a modern reader take it as anything more than devotional poetry?
      The purport itself anticipates this. Śrīdhara Svāmī and Viśvanātha Cakravartī are explicit — there was no discharge of semen; Sanātana Gosvāmī describes it as an awakening of consciousness within Vasudeva. The ācāryas are not naïve about biology; they are making a precise philosophical claim. The Lord is already viśvātmā — present in everyone's heart as īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṁ hṛd-deśe (BG 18.61). His 'appearance' is not a new arrival but a manifestation of what was always there. The Gauḍīya teacher does not flinch from the literal reading, but also insists this is not 'biology vs. miracle' — it is the unborn (aja) Lord appearing as if born (jāto bhagavān, SB 3.2.15). Reduce it to poetry and you have lost the personalist Kṛṣṇa; reduce it to mere physics and you have lost the ajaḥ. Both refusals are required.
    • If Kṛṣṇa is the Supersoul of all living entities — viśvātmā — then He is equally inside me, inside my dog, inside a mosquito. So why all the fuss about Vasudeva? My heart is just as much His residence.
      Yes, He is equally present — and that is precisely the tragedy the purport names: 'because of forgetfulness of this object, people are suffering in this material world.' The Lord's presence is universal; the devotee's receptivity is not. Vasudeva is distinguished not because Kṛṣṇa favored him geographically but because his consciousness was bhakta — abhayaṅkaraḥ applies to him because he had become a devotee. The Supersoul is in the mosquito too, but the mosquito does not become a vessel for the Lord's manifestation. The lesson is not 'Kṛṣṇa already lives in me, so I'm fine' — that is impersonalist drift. The lesson is: He is here; am I the kind of mind in which He can āviveśa — manifest? That requires sādhana, surrender, and the cultivation of bhakti, not a metaphysical shrug.

    While carrying the form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead within the core of his heart, Vasudeva bore the Lord’s transcendentally illuminating effulgence, and thus he became as bright as the sun. He was therefore very difficult to see or approach through sensory perception. Indeed, he was unapproachable and unperceivable even for such formidable men as Kaṁsa, and not only for Kaṁsa but for all living entities.
    Purport

    The word dhāma is significant. Dhāma refers to the place where the Supreme Personality of Godhead resides. In the beginning of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (1.1.1) it is said, dhāmnā svena sadā nirasta-kuhakaṁ satyaṁ paraṁ dhīmahi. In the abode of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, there is no influence of material energy ( dhāmnā svena sadā nirasta-kuhakam ). Any place where the Supreme Personality of Godhead is present by His name, form, qualities or paraphernalia immediately becomes a dhāma. For example, we speak of Vṛndāvana-dhāma, Dvārakā-dhāma and Mathurā-dhāma because in these places the name, fame, qualities and paraphernalia of the Supreme Godhead are always present. Similarly, if one is empowered by the Supreme Personality of Godhead to do something, the core of his heart becomes a dhāma, and thus he becomes so extraordinarily powerful that not only his enemies but also people in general are astonished to observe his activities. Because he is unapproachable, his enemies are simply struck with wonder, as explained here by the words durāsado ’tidurdharsaḥ. The words pauruṣaṁ dhāma have been explained by various ācāryas. Śrī Vīrarāghava Ācārya says that these words refer to the effulgence of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Vijayadhvaja says that they signify viṣṇu-tejas, and Śukadeva says bhagavat-svarūpa. The Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī says that these words indicate the influence of the Supreme Lord’s effulgence, and Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura says that they signify the appearance of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    While carrying the form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead within the core of his heart, Vasudeva bore the Lord's transcendentally illuminating effulgence, and thus he became as bright as the sun. He was therefore very difficult to see or approach through sensory perception. Indeed, he was unapproachable and unperceivable even for such formidable men as Kaṁsa, and not only for Kaṁsa but for all living entities.
    Commentary

    Vasudeva was holding the power (dhama) of the Lord (paurusam) . Or it can mean "Vasudeva became effulgent on seeing the appearance of the Lord within himself." According to the Visvakosa, dhama means, body, house, ray, place, birth and influence. Durasadah means that other living entities could not approach him. Ati durdharsa means that Kamsa and others could not defeat him.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Vasudeva took on the effulgence of the Lord (pauruṣaṁ dhāma) because the Lord’s power appeared in his mind. Or dhāma can mean manifestation or power. Viśva-kośa says that dhāṁa means body, house, rays, place, birth or power. People could not approach him or look at him (durāsadaḥ) and it was impossible to defeat him. This clearly (ha) happened in a pronounced way (sam).

    Concepts
    Jiva
    Personal Guidance
    When you carry Kṛṣṇa in the core of your heart, His dhāma shines through you — even your fiercest enemies cannot touch what He protects.
    Practical Applications
    • Begin the day by consciously installing Kṛṣṇa in the core of your heart through japa, and return to that seat whenever you feel exposed or afraid.
    • Notice when you try to protect yourself through image, argument, or aggression — and instead let the Lord's presence within be your real shield today.
    • Refuse to measure your strength by what others can see; serve quietly in one task today, trusting that the dhāma you carry within is the only durāsada power that matters.
    Reflection Questions
    • What in my life — a service, a responsibility, a relationship — am I empowered by Kṛṣṇa to carry, and am I bearing it with the gravitas of a dhāma or treating it as merely my own clever doing?
    • Where do I shrink from being 'durāsada' — unapproachable to flattery, gossip, or compromise — because I would rather be liked by Kaṁsa-like influences than guarded by the Lord's effulgence within?
    For Each Age Group
    youth
    • Pick the one social-media app that most easily 'approaches' you — the one that reads your moods and pulls you in. For one week, log out of it on your phone entirely; let your heart be a little less easy to walk into. Notice what tries to fill the space.
    • Before your next exam or big submission, spend two minutes silently placing Kṛṣṇa in the core of your heart and offering the work to Him. Then go in. Watch how differently peer panic, comparison, and the urge to cheat or copy actually land on you when you are not the one carrying the result.
    • Identify the one friend or group chat that most easily talks you out of your sva-dharma as a student — late nights, gossip, pulling you down when you try to study or chant. You do not need to break the friendship; you need to become slightly durāsada in that one direction. Practice one clear, kind 'no' this week without explanation or apology.
    householder
    • Before any significant family decision this week — a purchase, a school choice, a difficult conversation with your spouse — pause and consciously place Kṛṣṇa in the core of your heart first. Make the decision from that seat, not from fear, in-laws' opinions, or LinkedIn-style comparison with other families.
    • Your children and colleagues are constantly trying to 'read' you — to find which lever (guilt, flattery, anger, money) gets the response they want. For one week, practice being lovingly durāsada to manipulation: warm in presence, unmoved by leverage. Notice which family member is most disturbed by this; that is your diagnostic.
    • Make one room or corner of your home an actual dhāma — Deities or a picture of Kṛṣṇa, a clean āsana, your japa-mālā, no phones. Sit there for fifteen minutes every morning before the household wakes. The home that has a dhāma at its center cannot be approached by māyā in the same way as one that does not.
    senior
    • You are now closer than ever to the next 'transition' the body will make. Begin treating your heart, not your bank account or property file, as the most important asset to be in order — daily japa, hearing Bhāgavatam, association of devotees. This is the dhāma you actually carry across.
    • Younger family members are watching to see whether a life of sādhana produces something visibly different at the end. Without preaching, let your composure around illness, loss, and money decisions become its own quiet teaching — a pauruṣaṁ dhāma they cannot quite argue with.
    • Identify the two or three attachments — a property dispute, an old grievance, an identity as 'the one who provides' — that still make you very approachable to anxiety and anger. Name them aloud before the Deity each morning and consciously hand them to Kṛṣṇa. Loosening these now is how the heart becomes light enough to actually hold Him at the time of leaving.
    Common Pitfalls
    • Reading Vasudeva's effulgence as a metaphor for personal charisma or self-confidence, and then cultivating ahaṅkāra-driven 'presence' instead of carrying Kṛṣṇa within the heart.
    • Assuming that because the Lord empowers His devotee, one can court danger or provoke Kaṁsa-figures recklessly — forgetting that Vasudeva still moved with vairāgya, hrīḥ, and discretion, not bravado.
    • Treating 'unapproachable to sensory perception' as license to become aloof, cold, or socially withdrawn from family and duties, when the verse points to spiritual inaccessibility to envy and exploitation, not to ordinary human warmth.
    Discussion Prompts
    • Vasudeva became 'unapproachable' the moment Kṛṣṇa entered the core of his heart. Share with your partner: when have you seen someone whose inner life made them genuinely difficult to manipulate or sway — and how did that differ from mere stubbornness or arrogance? Where would you, honestly, still be easy to approach in the wrong way?
    • The verse says Vasudeva was unperceivable 'even for such formidable men as Kaṁsa.' Disagree productively: is this a literal protective effulgence, or is the Bhāgavatam describing a sober psychological reality — that those carrying Kṛṣṇa within cannot be read by purely materially-motivated people? Pick a side and defend it.
    • Prabhupāda says the heart of an empowered devotee itself becomes a dhāma. If that is true, what specifically in your daily routine is currently making your heart un-dhāma-like — what guests are you hosting there instead? Be concrete with your partner; no spiritual abstractions allowed.
    Role Play

    Two students. Student A is a devotee who has been quietly deepening sādhana for six months — more japa, less social media, fewer late-night outings. Student B is an old friend (the 'Kaṁsa' figure in miniature — not evil, just materially calibrated) who senses the change and shows up to 'check in,' actually trying to pull A back into the old group dynamics: 'You've gotten weird, you used to be fun, are you in a cult?' A must respond from the dhāma-bhāva of this verse — not defensive, not preachy, not apologetic, but genuinely durāsada (hard to grab onto) without being cold. Run it for five minutes, then swap. Debrief: where did A leak? Where did A's effulgence actually show?

    Objections & Responses
    • This sounds like spiritual narcissism dressed up in Sanskrit. 'I am so full of God that ordinary people can't even perceive me' — isn't this exactly the kind of self-flattery that makes religious people insufferable?
      A fair worry, and the verse itself protects against it. Notice: Vasudeva does not declare his own effulgence — the Bhāgavatam describes it, and Vasudeva himself behaves with extraordinary humility, even bowing to Kaṁsa to save the child. The dhāma is not his; he is carrying Kṛṣṇa. The moment a sādhaka thinks 'I have become unapproachable,' the dhāma has already left, because ahaṅkāra has moved back in. The test of real pauruṣaṁ dhāma is the opposite of narcissism — it is the quiet inability to be flattered, frightened, or bought. If someone is loudly inaccessible, that is just rajas with a tilak. Real durāsada looks, from the outside, simply like a person you cannot quite use.
    • The verse implies Kṛṣṇa is a localized person who 'enters' a heart and emits literal light. Modern readers will say this is mythological — surely the deeper meaning is that we all already have a divine spark, and 'Kṛṣṇa within' is just a colorful way of pointing to that universal Self.
      The Gauḍīya line will respectfully but firmly decline that translation. Prabhupāda is precise here: dhāma means the place where the Supreme Personality of Godhead resides, and Kṛṣṇa is a person — sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha — not a metaphor for an impersonal Self we already are. If 'Kṛṣṇa within' simply meant the divine spark every jīva already carries, then Vasudeva would have looked like the sun his entire life, and so would Kaṁsa. The whole point of the verse is that something new happened — the Supreme Person, by His own will, took residence — and that this is categorically different from the eternal ātman every living being already possesses. Collapsing the two erases bhakti, because you cannot surrender to, serve, or love a 'spark within yourself.' You can only do that with a Person who is other than you and dearer than you.

    Thereafter, accompanied by plenary expansions, the fully opulent Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is all-auspicious for the entire universe, was transferred from the mind of Vasudeva to the mind of Devakī. Devakī, having thus been initiated by Vasudeva, became beautiful by carrying Lord Kṛṣṇa, the original consciousness for everyone, the cause of all causes, within the core of her heart, just as the east becomes beautiful by carrying the rising moon.
    Purport

    As indicated here by the word manastaḥ, the Supreme Personality of Godhead was transferred from the core of Vasudeva’s mind or heart to the core of the heart of Devakī. We should note carefully that the Lord was transferred to Devakī not by the ordinary way for a human being, but by dīkṣā, initiation. Thus the importance of initiation is mentioned here. Unless one is initiated by the right person, who always carries within his heart the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one cannot acquire the power to carry the Supreme Godhead within the core of one’s own heart. The word acyutāṁśam is used because the Supreme Personality of Godhead is ṣaḍ-aiśvarya-pūrṇa, full in the opulences of wealth, strength, fame, knowledge, beauty and renunciation. The Supreme Godhead is never separated from His personal opulences. As stated in the Brahma-saṁhitā (5.39) , rāmādi-mūrtiṣu kalā-niyamena tiṣṭhan: the Lord is always situated with all His plenary expansions, such as Rāma, Nṛsiṁha and Varāha. Therefore the word acyutāṁśam is specifically used here, signifying that the Lord is always present with His plenary expansions and opulences. There is no need to think of the Lord artificially as yogīs do. Dhyānāvasthita-tad-gatena manasā paśyanti yaṁ yoginaḥ ( Bhāg. 12.13.1 ). Yogīs meditate upon the Supreme Person within the mind. For a devotee, however, the Lord is present, and His presence need only be awakened through initiation by a bona fide spiritual master. The Lord did not need to live within the womb of Devakī, for His presence within the core of her heart was sufficient to carry Him. One is here forbidden to think that Kṛṣṇa was begotten by Vasudeva within the womb of Devakī and that she carried the child within her womb. When Vasudeva was sustaining the form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead within his heart, he appeared just like the glowing sun, whose shining rays are always unbearable and scorching to the common man. The form of the Lord situated in the pure, unalloyed heart of Vasudeva is not different from the original form of Kṛṣṇa. The appearance of the form of Kṛṣṇa anywhere, and specifically within the heart, is called dhāma. Dhāma refers not only to Kṛṣṇa’s form, but to His name, His form, His quality and His paraphernalia. Everything becomes manifest simultaneously. Thus the eternal form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead with full potencies was transferred from the mind of Vasudeva to the mind of Devakī, exactly as the setting sun’s rays are transferred to the full moon rising in the east. Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, entered the body of Devakī from the body of Vasudeva. He was beyond the conditions of the ordinary living entity. When Kṛṣṇa is there, it is to be understood that all His plenary expansions, such as Nārāyaṇa, and incarnations like Lord Nṛsiṁha and Varāha, are with Him, and they are not subject to the conditions of material existence. In this way, Devakī became the residence of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is one without a second and the cause of all creation. Devakī became the residence of the Absolute Truth, but because she was within the house of Kaṁsa, she looked just like a suppressed fire, or like misused education. When fire is covered by the walls of a pot or is kept in a jug, the illuminating rays of the fire cannot be very much appreciated. Similarly, misused knowledge, which does not benefit the people in general, is not very much appreciated. So Devakī was kept within the prison walls of Kaṁsa’s palace, and no one could see her transcendental beauty, which resulted from her conceiving the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Commenting upon this verse, Śrī Vīrarāghava Ācārya writes: vasudeva-devakī jaṭharayor hṛdayayor bhagavataḥ sambandhaḥ. The Supreme Lord’s entrance into the womb of Devakī from the heart of Vasudeva was a heart-to-heart relationship.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Thereafter, accompanied by plenary expansions, the fully opulent Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is all-auspicious for the entire universe, was transferred from the mind of Vasudeva to the mind of Devakī. Devakī, having thus been initiated by Vasudeva, became beautiful by carrying Lord Kṛṣṇa, the original consciousness for everyone, the cause of all causes, within the core of her heart, just as the east becomes beautiful by carrying the rising moon.
    Commentary

    Then the Lord entered into Devaki from Vasudeva. This is described in this verse. She took into her mind that person who is the very form of auspiciousness for the whole universe, who does not deviate, and who includes all expansions such as Narayana and narasimha (jagan mangalam acyutamsam), who gives happiness (ka) to the minds (atma) of all the devotees and Siva (sarva), who appears (bhuta) on his own, independently (atma). The Lord appeared in devaki’s mind without the effort that yogis exert. Manastah dadhara mean she held with the mind. By saying this, material conception and birth is ruled out. A suitable example is given to support this. It was just like the eastern direction (kastha) holding the full moon (anandakara). It is understood that several days later she could perceive Krsna in her womb for it is said later " disty amba te kuksi gatah parah puman. (By fortune, o lady, the supreme Lord has entered your womb.)

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    She held the Lords (sarvātmakam) who appeared within her (ātmā-bhūtam) as her son. This indicates that the Lord does not take birth like jīvas. Madhva quotes from Tantra-bhagavata. aheyam anupādeyaṁ yad rūpam nityam avyayam sa evāpekṣa-rūpasya vyaktim evan janārdanaḥ agṛhnād vyasṛjac ceti kṛṣna-rāmādikāṁ tanum paṭhyate bhagavān īṣo mūḍa-buddhi-vyapekṣayā tamaṣā hy upagūḍasya yat tamaḥ pānam īśituḥ etat puruṣa-rūpasya grahaṇaṁ samudīryate kṛṣṇa-rāmādi rūpāṇāṁ loke vyakti-vyapekṣayā The foolish person covered by ignorance says that the Lord whose forms like Rāma and Kṛṣṇa are eternal and unchanging, incomparable, and without any faults accepts and gives up bodies. On seeing the appearance of Kṛṣṇa or Rāma in the world he declares that they accept material human forms. Mahā-varāha Purāṇa says: sarve nityāḥa śāśvatāś ca dehās tasya parātmanaḥ heyopadheya-rahitā naiva prakṛti-jāḥ kvacit paramānanda-sandohā jṣāna-mātraś ca sarvataḥ All the forms of God have eternal bodies without any faults. They never arise from matter. They are completely filled with the highest bliss and knowledge. This is the definition of the Lord. He was like the moon which gives bliss because of its sweet rays. The rest is according to the explanation of Śrīdhara Svāmī. Or, acyutāṁśam can mean “he who is not lacking even on part: he who is complete with all his parts, Bhagavān.” Therefore he is the root form (ātmā-bhūtam) who makes his appearance as if offering himself (samāhitam). It was previously mentioned that the seventh child would be the cause of joy and lamentation. The appearance of Kṛṣṇa was a cause of only joy. He was the cause of joy (ka) for all jīvas (sarvātma). Or he would appear personally (ātmā-bhūtam), unlike other forms which become the object of yogīs’ meditation with great effort because he appeared on his own (samāhitam).

    Concepts
    Jiva
    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa is received not by birth or biology but heart-to-heart through dīkṣā — a bona fide guru transmits Him from his heart into yours.
    Practical Applications
    • Identify whether you have taken shelter of a bona fide spiritual master who carries Kṛṣṇa in his heart, and if not, begin the search seriously today.
    • Refuse the yogic notion that you must imagine or manufacture Kṛṣṇa within — instead, prepare your heart through hearing and chanting so His already-present form can be awakened.
    • Notice where, like Devakī within Kaṁsa's prison, your inner cultivation is hidden by hostile surroundings, and protect that inner fire with daily sādhana rather than display.
    Reflection Questions
    • Whose heart am I actually drawing Kṛṣṇa from — am I trying to 'meditate Him up' on my own, or am I receiving Him through a bona fide channel of dīkṣā?
    • Like Devakī in Kaṁsa's prison, where in my life is my inner cultivation of Kṛṣṇa being kept hidden by hostile surroundings — and am I tending that inner fire anyway, or letting the walls extinguish it?
    For Each Age Group
    youth
    • Notice how much of your 'spiritual life' lives in your own head — playlists, reels, books, late-night thoughts. This week, find one living person senior to you in bhakti (a temple devotee, a teacher, an elder in your family) and actually sit with them for an hour; bhakti is transmitted, not downloaded.
    • Devakī carried the Lord even inside Kaṁsa's prison. Your campus, your hostel, your group chat is your Kaṁsa's palace — stop waiting until you 'get out' to begin sādhana. Fix one daily anchor (sixteen rounds is a long arc; start with one round and one verse) that travels with you regardless of environment.
    • Watch the pull to perform your inner life on social media — the suppressed fire is more powerful than the displayed one. For one month, keep your japa, your reading, and any darśana strictly off your feed; let your devotion stay covered like Devakī in the prison and observe what changes inside.
    householder
    • Your home is the heart-chamber where Kṛṣṇa is meant to be carried. Concretely: install or re-install your home altar this week, and commit with your spouse to one fixed family program — a short ārati, one verse read aloud, prasāda offered — every single day, treating the household itself as Devakī's heart.
    • On the question of dīkṣā: if you have not yet formally taken shelter of a bona fide spiritual master in the paramparā, stop deferring it as 'something for later when life settles.' Identify the line, the teacher, the community, and take a real step this quarter — your children are watching whether bhakti, in your life, is theoretical or transmitted.
    • In your career and money decisions, ask whether what you are building is a Kaṁsa's palace (impressive walls hiding a suppressed fire) or a Vasudeva's heart (modest outwardly, but actually carrying the Lord). Make one concrete adjustment — a job, a purchase, a school decision — where you choose the second over the first this year.
    senior
    • Your role now is Vasudeva's role — to transfer, heart to heart, what you have been carrying. Identify by name two or three younger people (children, grandchildren, juniors, mentees) and commit to a regular, unhurried transmission — read one verse with them weekly, tell them the pastimes Prabhupāda told you, let your bhakti actually leave your body before it does.
    • Loosen the grip on the 'prison walls' of property, position, and reputation that you have spent decades building. This year, formally hand over one major responsibility (a business, a trust, a household role) to the next generation — not because you are incapable, but to free your heart to be, like Devakī's, only the residence of the Lord.
    • Mortality is now close enough to be honest about. Each evening, before sleep, place Kṛṣṇa consciously in the core of your heart with the same deliberateness with which Vasudeva transferred Him to Devakī — so that when the body finally falls, the transfer at the moment of death is only the continuation of a transfer you have already been practicing for years.
    Common Pitfalls
    • Treating initiation as a social ceremony or sentimental milestone, rather than the actual transmission by which the Lord is established in the heart — and then wondering why no inner transformation follows.
    • Imitating the yogī's manufactured meditation — trying to 'visualize' Kṛṣṇa into the heart by mental effort — instead of awakening the personal Lord, complete with His name, form, qualities and paraphernalia, through the mercy of a bona fide guru.
    • Reducing acyutāṁśam to a bare 'inner divine spark' or impersonal presence, forgetting that Kṛṣṇa is never separated from His ṣaḍ-aiśvarya and His plenary expansions — and thereby drifting into the impersonalist substitute the verse explicitly forbids.
    Discussion Prompts
    • Prabhupāda insists Kṛṣṇa was transferred from Vasudeva to Devakī by dīkṣā, not by ordinary conception, and that without initiation by a bona fide spiritual master one cannot carry the Lord in the heart. Where does this leave the modern practitioner who reads, chants, and feels devotion but has not formally accepted a guru? Push each other — is unintiated bhakti merely preparatory, or is the verse making a stronger claim?
    • Devakī, even while carrying the Supreme Personality of Godhead in her heart, looked outwardly like a 'suppressed fire' inside Kaṁsa's prison. Share with your partner one area of your present life that feels like Kaṁsa's prison — and disagree honestly about whether the right response is to escape it, transform it, or simply carry Kṛṣṇa within it as Devakī did.
    • The purport draws a sharp line between the yogī who must artificially construct the Lord's form in meditation and the devotee in whom the Lord's presence is awakened by the spiritual master. Does this distinction still hold today, when meditation apps, visualization techniques, and 'consciousness work' are everywhere? Where do members of your group catch themselves drifting into yogic self-effort instead of receptive devotion?
    Role Play

    Two students pair up. Student A plays a sincere seeker who has been chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa for two years, reads Prabhupāda's books daily, and feels Kṛṣṇa in the heart — but has never formally taken initiation, arguing that 'my relationship with Kṛṣṇa is direct, I do not need a middleman.' Student B plays a senior devotee who has just heard SB 10.2.18 in class and must, without being preachy or condescending, explain why this verse specifically forbids that view — that the heart-to-heart transmission Vīrarāghava Ācārya describes (vasudeva-devakī jaṭharayor hṛdayayor bhagavataḥ sambandhaḥ) requires a living link. Run it for seven minutes, then switch roles. Afterward, each pair reports the strongest objection they could not answer.

    Objections & Responses
    • This whole verse reads like mythology dressed up as theology — a baby mystically transferred from one mind to another, sustained without a womb. A modern reader cannot take this literally, and once we read it as metaphor the theological claims about initiation collapse with it.
      The verse is not asking you to first accept a biological miracle and then derive a doctrine from it. It is describing the descent of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is by definition not subject to the conditions of material existence — Prabhupāda is explicit that Kṛṣṇa 'was beyond the conditions of the ordinary living entity.' The metaphysics comes first: if Kṛṣṇa is acyuta and ṣaḍ-aiśvarya-pūrṇa, then the manner of His appearance need not, and will not, conform to ordinary gestation. The 'mythological' reading flattens this into a folk tale precisely because it has already smuggled in the assumption that only the empirically ordinary is real. The Gauḍīya answer is that the verse is teaching us the opposite: the Absolute can act personally and specifically without being reduced to our categories, and this is exactly why dīkṣā — a heart-to-heart transmission, not a biological one — is the model for how He enters a devotee.
    • Saying that one cannot carry Kṛṣṇa in the heart without being initiated by a bona fide spiritual master sounds like institutional gatekeeping. It conveniently makes the institution indispensable and dismisses every sincere bhakta outside the line.
      Hear the verse carefully — it is not the institution that is indispensable, it is the living link. Vasudeva did not transfer Kṛṣṇa to Devakī because he held an office; he did it because he himself was actually carrying the Lord 'like the glowing sun' in his unalloyed heart. Prabhupāda's standard is exactly the same: 'unless one is initiated by the right person, who always carries within his heart the Supreme Personality of Godhead.' That cuts against institutional complacency as sharply as it cuts against do-it-yourself spirituality. The point is not that a stamped certificate gives you Kṛṣṇa, nor that your private sincerity does — it is that bhakti is by nature received, transmitted heart to heart, the way a flame is lit from a flame. To object to that is, in the end, to insist that the disciple be his own source — and a source you generate yourself is, by definition, not the Supreme.

    Devakī then kept within herself the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the cause of all causes, the foundation of the entire cosmos, but because she was under arrest in the house of Kaṁsa, she was like the flames of a fire covered by the walls of a pot, or like a person who has knowledge but cannot distribute it to the world for the benefit of human society.
    Purport

    In this verse the word jñāna-khala is most significant. Knowledge is meant for distribution. Although there is already much scientific knowledge, whenever scientists or philosophers awaken to a particular type of knowledge, they try to distribute it throughout the world, for otherwise the knowledge gradually dries up and no one benefits from it. India has the knowledge of Bhagavad-gītā, but unfortunately, for some reason or other, this sublime knowledge of the science of God was not distributed throughout the world, although it is meant for all of human society. Therefore Kṛṣṇa Himself appeared as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and ordered all Indians to take up the cause of distributing the knowledge of Bhagavad-gītā throughout the entire world. yāre dekha, tāre kaha ‘kṛṣṇa’-upadeśa āmāra ājñāya guru hañā tāra’ ei deśa “Instruct everyone to follow the orders of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa as they are given in Bhagavad-gītā and Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam. In this way become a spiritual master and try to liberate everyone in this land.” (Cc. Madhya 7.128) Although India has the sublime knowledge of Bhagavad-gītā, Indians have not done their proper duty of distributing it. Now, therefore, the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement has been set up to distribute this knowledge as it is, without distortion. Although previously there were attempts to distribute the knowledge of Bhagavad-gītā, these attempts involved distortion and compromise with mundane knowledge. But now the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, without mundane compromises, is distributing Bhagavad-gītā as it is, and people are deriving the benefits of awakening to Kṛṣṇa consciousness and becoming devotees of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Therefore the proper distribution of knowledge has begun by which not only will the whole world benefit, but India’s glory will be magnified in human society. Kaṁsa tried to arrest Kṛṣṇa consciousness within his house ( bhojendra-gehe ), with the result that Kaṁsa, with all his opulences, was later vanquished. Similarly, the real knowledge of Bhagavad-gītā was being choked by unscrupulous Indian leaders, with the result that India’s culture, and knowledge of the Supreme were being lost. Now, however, because Kṛṣṇa consciousness is spreading, the proper use of Bhagavad-gītā is being attempted.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Devakī then kept within herself the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the cause of all causes, the foundation of the entire cosmos, but because she was under arrest in the house of Kaṁsa, she was like the flames of a fire covered by the walls of a pot, or like a person who has knowledge but cannot distribute it to the world for the benefit of human society.
    Commentary

    Devaki became the shelter of the shelter of all material and non-material worlds, but all people could not take advantage of that bliss-giving form. Only a few close persons could appreciate her condition. In the prison house of Kamsa (bhojendra) she was like a covered fire. When a fire is burning in a house, it does not illuminate the town, but only the objects or persons near it in the house. However when the fire becomes strong it can burn down the restricting house. In this way, Devaki also would in due time destroy Kamsa. Knowledge (sarasvati) trapped in the hearts of men who do not distribute it (literally, cheaters of knowledge) does not flourish and benefit others. That knowledge will eventually destroy its restrictor, who is very sinful. In the same way Devaki would destroy offensive Kamsa.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The word jagat means “that which moves.” Thus it means temporary. Thus sarva-jagat means everything temporary. However by taking sarva as a separate indicator, sarva (all) can also indicate entities which are eternal. Thus sarva-jagan-nivāsa means the Lord who is the shelter of eternal and temporary beings. As the śruti says yasya bhāsā sarvam idam; vibhāti: by his light everything illuminates. (Śvetaśvatāra Upaniṣad) This indicates Kṛṣṇa. Devakī acted as his shelter (nivāsa-bhūtā). But though she was thus qualified to be the giver of all bliss and auspiciousness, she did not shine externally with those qualities but shone internally with her own bliss which excelled that of Vasudeva and others. A covered flame and a person with suppressed knowledge do not shine with all brilliance but shine with brightness internally. These two by their light give internal light because of their personal splendor. For the person in knowledge, the internal aspect is the mind. Even if a flame is covered it can burn down a house. Covered knowledge destroys its shelter (the subtle body) along with sin.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    She had become the supreme shelter of Kṛṣna who is the shelter of the whole universe. She appeared in this world as the mother of svayam bhagavān. She was most fortunate and most beautiful because of this. Still, she did not shine or appear beautiful (na reje). She was like a covered fire since she was not happy. An example is given. She was like person who is the personification of the Vedas (sarasvatī), who does not reveal the knowledge to others (jṣāna-khale). Though being happy in himself with that knowledge, a person deprives another person of knowledge. Hiding knowledge however does not depend on being in Kaṁsa’s prison. (Thus it is a general example.) Or knowledge attained by a person whose intention is to harm others (jṣāna-khale) does not shine. The defect is in the receptacle of knowledge (being within the prison). Bhojendra-gehe can also mean “in the kitchen.” Just as a flame, covered by smoke in the kitchen, does not shine, so she did not shine because of Kaṁsa’s evil actions. Or did she not shine constantly, being imprisoned by Kaṁsa? Yes, she shone because she contained the lord. Just as a flame shines even though repressed, she shone. Similarly a person with great knowledge shines constantly, by special cleverness through suggestion and other devices of speech (jṣāna-khale).

    Concepts
    JivaGuru
    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa-knowledge withheld is like fire trapped in a pot — receive it from your guru and pass it on, or it dies in you.
    Practical Applications
    • Identify one person in your life who could benefit from something you have learned about Kṛṣṇa, and share it plainly with them today.
    • Refuse the impulse to hoard sādhana as a private comfort — speak one verse or teaching aloud to someone before the day ends.
    • Notice where you have been a jñāna-khala — withholding what you know out of shyness or self-importance — and break the pattern in one concrete conversation.
    Reflection Questions
    • What kṛṣṇa-conscious knowledge has Kṛṣṇa already placed within me — through hearing, reading, or association — that I am keeping 'arrested in the Bhojendra-gehe' of my private life instead of distributing to those around me?
    • Where am I behaving like the jñāna-khala — guarding what I have received as personal capital — and who in my immediate circle is being deprived because of that withholding?
    For Each Age Group
    youth
    • Pick one thing you've actually understood from Gītā or Bhāgavatam study and say it out loud this week to one non-devotee friend — not as a lecture, just one sentence in a real conversation. Notice the fear that rises (looking weird, losing status in the friend group); that fear is the wall of Kaṁsa's house.
    • Audit your social media for one week: how much of what you post is curated self-image (Kaṁsa's opulence) versus anything that points to Kṛṣṇa or to the soul? You don't have to start posting verses — but notice how much energy goes into the prison and how little into the flame.
    • When a classmate is breaking down before exams or after a breakup, resist two reflexes — (a) the secular reflex of 'you do you, follow your truth,' and (b) the preachy reflex of quoting verses at them. Instead, sit with them, then offer one concrete thing rooted in sva-dharma: a walk, a meal, a question about what actually matters. That is karuṇā in your stage of life.
    householder
    • Your children are watching what you protect and what you transmit. This week, name one piece of Kṛṣṇa-conscious understanding you have been keeping behind the walls of 'they're too young' or 'my spouse won't like it' — and find one age-appropriate way to share it (a story at dinner, a verse on the fridge, a question in the car). Jñāna-khala begins at home.
    • In your professional life, identify the one place where you compromise the truth you know — softening, omitting, going along — to keep the income or the relationship intact. Don't quit the job. But this week, in one meeting or one family decision, speak the thing you would have swallowed. Test whether the walls were as load-bearing as you thought.
    • Look at how you spend money on the family. How much goes to maintaining the bhojendra-gehe (the comfortable house, the optics, the schools that signal status), and how much actually flows toward distributing Kṛṣṇa — books, prasāda for guests, supporting a temple, hosting a kīrtana? Re-balance one line item this month.
    senior
    • You have decades of realization that younger devotees and family members need. Identify one specific person — a grandchild, a younger colleague at the temple, a neighbor — who would receive what you have to give, and schedule a recurring time with them. Do not wait to be asked; Devakī was not asked either, and the cost of her silence was the world's loss.
    • Begin to dismantle the walls of your own bhojendra-gehe before death does it for you. Choose one possession, one grudge, or one identity (former title, former role, former grievance) and actively release it this month. Notice that as the walls come down, the flame Devakī carried — the same Kṛṣṇa within you — has more room to be seen by others.
    • Write down, in your own hand, the three things about Kṛṣṇa and this path you most do not want to die without having said clearly to your children and grandchildren. Don't aestheticize it, don't make it a memoir — just the three things. Then find the occasion, however ordinary, to say them. Legacy in this line is not what you owned; it is what of Kṛṣṇa got out of the house through you.
    Common Pitfalls
    • Treating the verse as a license for aggressive proselytizing or correcting strangers, instead of the humble, relational distribution Caitanya Mahāprabhu modeled with 'yāre dekha, tāre kaha kṛṣṇa-upadeśa.'
    • Equating 'distribution' with social-media broadcasting or content production, while neglecting the harder work of speaking Kṛṣṇa-kathā to one's own family, classmates, and colleagues.
    • Distorting or diluting the message to make it palatable — the very compromise Prabhupāda warns against — and calling that 'distribution,' when in fact it choke s the knowledge just as surely as Kaṁsa's walls did.
    Discussion Prompts
    • Devakī held Kṛṣṇa within her but could not share Him because she was imprisoned by Kaṁsa. Where in your own life are you 'imprisoned' — by job, family expectation, fear of judgment, social media optics — such that the kṛṣṇa-jñāna you've received cannot get out? Be specific about the walls, not just the regret.
    • Prabhupāda calls the one who hoards knowledge a jñāna-khala — a miser of knowledge — and says such knowledge 'gradually dries up.' Disagree if you can: is there ever a legitimate case for keeping spiritual realization private (humility, lack of qualification, fear of misrepresenting), or is that always Kaṁsa's prison dressed up as virtue?
    • Prabhupāda says previous attempts to distribute the Gītā 'involved distortion and compromise with mundane knowledge.' In your own speaking about Kṛṣṇa — to coworkers, in-laws, skeptical friends — where do you compromise to make it palatable, and where is the line between skillful framing (upāya) and dilution (apa-siddhānta)?
    Role Play

    Two students pair up. Student A is a software engineer who has been chanting japa and reading Bhāgavatam for two years and has just been promoted to team lead at a secular tech company. A junior teammate confides she is suicidal after a breakup and asks, 'How do you stay so steady?' Student A has thirty seconds to respond. Student B plays the teammate. Run the scene three times: (1) A says nothing about Kṛṣṇa, only generic empathy — afterward, debrief whether that was karuṇā or cowardice; (2) A delivers a mini-lecture about the eternal soul — debrief whether that was distribution or jñāna-khala-style showing-off; (3) A speaks one sentence that points to Kṛṣṇa without using the word, and offers to talk more after work. Class then names which version was the bhojendra-gehe (Kaṁsa's house) and which was the open flame.

    Objections & Responses
    • Isn't 'distributing knowledge to the whole world' just religious imperialism in spiritual clothing? People have their own paths — who are we to evangelize the Gītā at them?
      Notice the verse's image: Devakī suffers because the knowledge cannot get out, and Prabhupāda compares it to a scientist who refuses to publish. We don't accuse the cancer researcher of imperialism for sharing her findings — we'd accuse her of cruelty if she didn't. The Gauḍīya position is that Kṛṣṇa is the actual proprietor of every living being (BG 5.29), so introducing someone to Him is restoring a relationship, not imposing a foreign one. The distortion to avoid is forcing or manipulating; the distortion equally to avoid is silence dressed up as tolerance. Real karuṇā speaks; false karuṇā stays comfortable.
    • Devakī's 'imprisonment' is just a poetic frame — the verse is mythology. The practical lesson about distributing knowledge feels grafted on by Prabhupāda to promote his own movement.
      Two things. First, the Bhāgavatam itself supplies the simile (sarasvatī jñāna-khale yathā satī) — Vyāsa, not Prabhupāda, equates Devakī's confinement with knowledge trapped in a miser. The application is in the verse, not added to it. Second, even read as story, the structure is exact: a tyrant (Kaṁsa / our own ahaṅkāra and social fear) tries to seal Kṛṣṇa inside four walls, and the result is the tyrant's destruction, not Kṛṣṇa's. Prabhupāda is doing what every ācārya in this line does — showing the verse is about you, today, not about a long-ago royal family. If it were only mythology, you would not be uncomfortable with the question.

    Because the Supreme Personality of Godhead was within her womb, Devakī illuminated the entire atmosphere in the place where she was confined. Seeing her jubilant, pure and smiling, Kaṁsa thought, “The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viṣṇu, who is now within her, will kill me. Devakī has never before looked so brilliant and jubilant.”
    Purport

    The Lord says in Bhagavad-gītā (4.7) : yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṁ sṛjāmy aham “Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious practice, O descendant of Bharata, and a predominant rise of irreligion — at that time I descend Myself.” In this age, at the present moment, there are inordinate discrepancies in the discharge of human duties. Human life is meant for God-realization, but unfortunately the materialistic civilization is stressing only the senses of the body, not understanding the living force within the body. As clearly stated in Bhagavad-gītā ( dehino ’smin yathā dehe ), within the body is the body’s proprietor, the living force, which is more important. But human society has become so fallen that instead of understanding the living force within the body, people have become busy with external things. This is a discrepancy in human duties. Therefore Kṛṣṇa has taken birth or taken shelter within the womb of the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement. Men of Kaṁsa’s class, therefore, are very much afraid and are busy trying to stop this movement, especially in the Western countries. One politician has remarked that the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is spreading like an epidemic and that if not checked immediately, within ten years it may capture governmental power. There is, of course, such potency in the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement. As stated by authorities (Cc. Ādi 17.22), kali-kāle nāma-rūpe kṛṣṇa-avatāra: in this age, Kṛṣṇa has appeared in the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra. The Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is spreading like wildfire all over the world, and it will go on doing so. Men who are like Kaṁsa are very much afraid of the movement’s progress and acceptance by the younger generation, but as Kṛṣṇa could not be killed by Kaṁsa, this movement cannot be checked by men of Kaṁsa’s class. The movement will go on increasing more and more, provided the leaders of the movement remain firmly Kṛṣṇa conscious by following the regulative principles and the primary activities of chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra regularly.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Because the Supreme Personality of Godhead was within her womb, Devakī illuminated the entire atmosphere in the place where she was confined. Seeing her jubilant, pure and smiling, Kaṁsa thought, "The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viṣṇu, who is now within her, will kill me. Devakī has never before looked so brilliant and jubilant."
    Commentary

    Devaki, who was holding Visnu within her womb (ajitantaram) , filled the room with light. She smiled out of genuine bliss (suci smitam), not in order to deceive Kamsa as previously. Seeing her, Kamsa then addressed her. Hari can mean lion. "Like the lion who kills (pranahari) the elephant, Hari, who will take my life, has taken shelter in the womb of Devaki. Certainly this is so, because (yat) she did not appear effulgent previously (pura)."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Kaṁsa personally saw her. Her effulgence is described in Viṣṇu Purāṇa: na śeke devakīṁ draṣṭum kaścid apy atitejasā jājvalyamānāṁ tāṁ dṛṣṭvā manāṁsi kṣobham āyayuḥ No one could look at Devakī because of her effulgence. Seeing her shining form they became disturbed in mind. Because of the bliss of the Lord she had a pure (śuci) smile. It was not a deceptive smile which she previously showed. Seeing her, Kaṁsa spoke. The Lord has taken shelter of her womb or heart (gūham.) A secondary meaning is: like a snake the Lord has taken shelter of a hole out of fear of me, a lion.

    Related values & verses
    Related values
    Shraddha (Faith / Reverence)Anahankarah (Freedom from False Ego)Tejas (Inner Radiance / Vigour)Mardava (Gentleness)Hrih (Modesty / Sense of Shame)

    Concepts
    Mantra
    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa within radiates through Devakī — when you shelter Him in your heart, your very presence threatens the Kaṁsa within and around you.
    Practical Applications
    • Chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra attentively today so that, like Devakī, your face carries the tejas of one who shelters Him within.
    • Notice the 'Kaṁsa-voice' inside that wants to suppress your sādhana out of fear, and refuse it by sitting for japa anyway.
    • Speak about Kṛṣṇa once today to someone in your life — trust that the same potency that frightened Kaṁsa is still active in His name.
    Reflection Questions
    • Devakī's tejas radiated outward because Kṛṣṇa was within her — what 'inner cargo' am I currently carrying (entertainment, anxieties, calculations) that is silently radiating from me and shaping how others perceive me?
    • Kaṁsa correctly diagnosed Devakī's brilliance but drew the demonic conclusion — where in my own life have I sensed a higher presence in someone or something and reacted with threat or suspicion rather than shelter?
    For Each Age Group
    youth
    • Audit your social media for one week with a single question: when you post, are you trying to radiate something real, or are you trying to manufacture the appearance of radiance for an audience? Devakī did not know she was glowing — Kaṁsa noticed. Stop curating; start chanting japa before you open the app.
    • Identify the Kaṁsa in your friend group — the one who reflexively mocks anyone who studies hard, prays, refuses to drink, or takes things seriously. Now identify the Kaṁsa in yourself: which friend's seriousness about Kṛṣṇa or studies makes you want to drag them down to your level? Confess that to a senior devotee this week.
    • Before your next exam or interview, take five minutes to chant and remember that the body is not the proprietor. You are not your GPA, your offer letter, or your follower count. Then do the work with full effort and zero attachment to the result — this is the karma-yoga the Gītā has been teaching since 2.47, applied to your actual Tuesday.
    householder
    • When your spouse, child, or co-worker shows a flash of genuine spiritual seriousness — a desire to chant more, to give to a temple, to take a vow — watch your own first reaction carefully. If it is anxiety, calculation, or the urge to talk them down ('let's be practical'), you have just met the Kaṁsa in yourself. Name it, do not act on it, and instead support their step.
    • Make one concrete family decision this month — about money, about your child's education, about your career — where you visibly choose the soul's interest over the body's comfort. Tell your spouse what you are doing and why, in plain language, without preaching. Real compassion serves the soul; material compassion just removes discomfort.
    • Light a lamp in your home shrine and chant audibly so your children hear it — not as performance, but as the household's actual atmosphere. Devakī's prison cell glowed because of who was within. Ask honestly: what is within the womb of your home, and what is it radiating to the children growing up inside it?
    senior
    • You have already passed through infancy, youth, householder life, and are now in a body the Gītā calls a transition, not an annihilation. Begin loosening one specific attachment this month — a possession, a grudge, a role you still cling to — and offer it explicitly to Kṛṣṇa. Practice the dhīra-bhāva of BG 2.13, not as theory, but as your actual daily disposition.
    • Identify two younger people — one in your family, one outside — who would benefit from hearing how Kṛṣṇa consciousness has actually held you through old age, illness, and loss. Do not lecture; tell the story plainly. Prabhupāda's purport ties the movement's continuation to leaders remaining firmly Kṛṣṇa conscious — your steadiness now is part of that transmission.
    • Sit with the verse's image: a body becomes radiant because of who is within. As your body weakens, ask whether the same is becoming more true or less true of you. If less, increase your chanting and reduce your consumption of news, opinion, and complaint — these are the materialistic 'external things' Prabhupāda names as the discrepancy of human duties.
    Common Pitfalls
    • Reading the verse as praise of Devakī's personal radiance and aspiring to 'glow' for its own sake, rather than recognizing the radiance as a sign that Kṛṣṇa Himself was within — confusing the lamp with the flame.
    • Applying the Kaṁsa-Kṛṣṇa contrast only to external 'opponents of the movement' while never auditing the Kaṁsa-like reflexes (envy, fear of being eclipsed, urge to suppress what is purer) operating within one's own heart.
    • Treating tejas, dhairya, and anahankāra as personality traits to cultivate through self-improvement techniques, instead of as natural symptoms that arise when one shelters Kṛṣṇa within through chanting and the regulative principles.
    Discussion Prompts
    • Devakī's body literally radiated because Kṛṣṇa was within her womb. In your own life, name one person you know whose presence visibly changes a room — and one person who drains it. What is actually being transmitted, and is it tejas or something else? Push each other: is 'good vibes' the same thing as the tejas Prabhupāda points to here, or is that a sentimental flattening?
    • Kaṁsa sees Devakī's brilliance and immediately reads it as a threat to himself. Share a time when someone else's spiritual progress made you uncomfortable, envious, or dismissive. Don't let your partner off with a polite answer — name the specific person and the specific feeling. What does the Kaṁsa-reaction reveal about the ahaṅkāra still operating in you?
    • Prabhupāda claims the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is 'Kṛṣṇa taking shelter within the womb' of the saṅkīrtana movement, and that Kaṁsa-class men try to stop it. Where do you find yourself genuinely siding with the Kaṁsa-class — wanting the movement softened, made more respectable, less embarrassing in public? Be honest with each other: where does your own reputation matter more to you than the movement's potency?
    Role Play

    Two students are paired. Student A is a longtime devotee who has just told their non-devotee sibling (Student B) that they are taking initiation, moving into the temple's outreach program, and giving up a lucrative job offer. Student B plays the sibling — affectionate, intelligent, secular, and genuinely worried that A is being 'captured' by what looks, from outside, like the kind of movement Prabhupāda's politician feared. Student B must press the real objections: cult dynamics, wasted education, family duty, the suspicion that A's new 'radiance' is just brainwashing. Student A must respond not with slogans but in the spirit of this verse — without attacking the sibling's good intentions, without retreating into defensiveness, and without softening Kṛṣṇa into a generic 'spiritual path.' After ten minutes, swap roles. Then debrief together: where did A sound like a real practitioner, and where did A sound like a recruiter? Where did B's objections actually land?

    Objections & Responses
    • Prabhupāda's purport reads like movement triumphalism — 'spreading like wildfire,' politicians afraid of us, governmental power within ten years. That was 1970s rhetoric and it didn't come true. Doesn't this date the purport and weaken the verse's authority?
      The historical prediction is not the point — the structural claim is. Prabhupāda is reading the verse as a pattern: wherever Kṛṣṇa takes shelter (in a womb, in a saṅkīrtana movement, in a sincere chanter), Kaṁsa-class consciousness reflexively tries to extinguish that light. That pattern is empirically observable today — in ourselves first, in institutions second. The 'ten years to governmental power' line is incidental; the diagnosis of materialistic civilization mistaking the body for the proprietor is exactly as accurate now as then. Read the purport as Prabhupāda reading the verse, not as Prabhupāda predicting elections. And note the conditional he closes with — 'provided the leaders remain firmly Kṛṣṇa conscious by following the regulative principles.' He explicitly ties the movement's potency to sādhana, not to demographics.
    • Devakī's radiance came from carrying Kṛṣṇa physically in her womb. That's a one-time pastime of the Supreme Lord. It is sentimental and frankly self-flattering for ordinary chanters to apply this to themselves and claim that we, too, are carrying Kṛṣṇa and shining.
      The objection is healthy — it guards against the impersonalist drift where every devotee imagines themselves a little Devakī. But the Gauḍīya answer is precise: we do not claim Devakī's position; we claim the principle Prabhupāda draws from the verse. Kali-kāle nāma-rūpe kṛṣṇa-avatāra — in this age Kṛṣṇa has appeared as the holy name. When the holy name takes shelter on the tongue and in the heart of a sincere chanter, something does change in the atmosphere around that chanter — not because the chanter is exalted, but because Kṛṣṇa Himself is non-different from His name. The tejas is His, not ours. The moment we begin to take credit for the radiance, we have already lost it — that is the ahaṅkāra Kaṁsa himself models in this very chapter. So the verse is not a flattery; it is a warning about whose light it actually is.

    Kaṁsa thought: What is my duty now? The Supreme Lord, who knows His purpose will not give up His prowess. Devakī is a woman, she is my sister, and moreover she is now pregnant. If I kill her, my reputation, opulence and duration of life will certainly be vanquished.
    Purport

    According to Vedic principles, a woman, a brāhmaṇa, an old man, a child and a cow should never be killed. It appears that Kaṁsa, although a great enemy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, was aware of the Vedic culture and conscious of the fact that the soul transmigrates from one body to another and that one suffers in the next life according to the karmas of this life. Therefore he was afraid of killing Devakī, since she was a woman, she was his sister, and she was pregnant. A kṣatriya becomes famous by performing heroic acts. But what would be heroic about killing a woman who, while confined in his custody, was under his shelter? Therefore, he did not want to act drastically by killing Devakī. Kaṁsa’s enemy was within Devakī’s womb, but killing an enemy in such a nescient state would not be an exhibition of prowess. According to kṣatriya rules, an enemy should be fought face to face and with proper weapons. Then if the enemy is killed, the victor becomes famous. Kaṁsa very conscientiously deliberated upon these facts and therefore refrained from killing Devakī, although he was completely confident that his enemy had already appeared within her womb.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Kaṁsa thought: What is my duty now? The Supreme Lord, who knows His purpose [paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṁ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām Bg. 4.8], will not give up His prowess. Devakī is a woman, she is my sister, and moreover she is now pregnant. If I kill her, my reputation, opulence and duration of life will certainly be vanquished.
    Commentary

    In this verse he speaks more clearly his intentions. "What should I do about Hari (tasmin)? Is it proper to kill him while he is still an embryo? No, because those interested in their own welfare (artha tantra) do not destroy their own good name. By killing him now my reputation of prowess will be destroyed. But if he is born and grows, and then I fight with him, whether I am victorious or defeated, my glory will remain intact. Killing a child in the womb is not an act of bravery. Not only will it destroy my fame, but dharma also gets destroyed." Thus he says by killing a woman, a sister, and a foetus, fame, power and lifespan will be permanently lost. This temporary restriction on his evil nature was because of fear. Thus he began thinking of his reputation through careful discrimination.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    (First meaning is: Viṣṇu will not give up his prowess and will try to kill me. But killing a woman is sinful.) According to Śrīdhara Svāmī there is a second meaning. “A person knowing his own benefit does not give up his prowess. Thus killing a woman is not good since one loses fame, wealth and longevity.” Right now, immediately what should I do? His evil nature became restricted because of fear, and he thought of how to act for his benefit. If I kill her, will it not be a temporary means to protect my life? If I kill her, will I not obtain long lasting infamy and loss of wealth? It is bad to kill a woman, worse if she is my sister, and worst if she is pregnant. And by killing her, it is bad to lose fame, worse to lose wealth and worst to lose long life. By killing her, my life is destroyed. What will be the good of that?
