    O Lord, cause of all causes, if Your transcendental body were not beyond the modes of material nature, one could not understand the difference between matter and transcendence. Only by Your presence can one understand the transcendental nature of Your Lordship, who are the controller of material nature. Your transcendental nature is very difficult to understand unless one is influenced by the presence of Your transcendental form.
    Purport

    It is said, traiguṇya-viṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna. Unless one is situated in transcendence, one cannot understand the transcendental nature of the Lord. As stated in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam (10.14.29) : athāpi te deva padāmbuja-dvaya- prasāda-leśānugṛhīta eva hi jānāti tattvaṁ bhagavan-mahimno na cānya eko ’pi ciraṁ vicinvan Only by the mercy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead can one understand Him. Those who are in the modes of material nature, although speculating for thousands of years, cannot understand Him. The Lord has innumerable forms ( rāmādi-mūrtiṣu kalā-niyamena tiṣṭhan ), and unless these forms, such as Lord Rāmacandra, Nṛsiṁhadeva, Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, were transcendental, how could they be worshiped by devotees since time immemorial? Bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaś cāsmi tattvataḥ ( Bg. 18.55 ). Devotees who awaken their transcendental nature in the presence of the Lord and who follow the rules and regulations of devotional service can understand Lord Kṛṣṇa, Lord Rāmacandra and other incarnations, who are not of this material world but who come from the spiritual world for the benefit of people in general. If one does not take to this process, one imagines or manufactures some form of God according to material qualities and can never awaken a real understanding of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. The words bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaś cāsmi tattvataḥ signify that unless one worships the Lord according to the regulative devotional principles, one cannot awaken the transcendental nature. Deity worship, even in the absence of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, awakens the transcendental nature of the devotee, who thus becomes increasingly attached to the Lord’s lotus feet. The appearance of Kṛṣṇa is the answer to all imaginative iconography of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Everyone imagines the form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead according to his mode of material nature. In the Brahma-saṁhitā it is said that the Lord is the oldest person. Therefore a section of religionists imagine that God must be very old, and therefore they depict a form of the Lord like a very old man. But in the same Brahma-saṁhitā, that is contradicted; although He is the oldest of all living entities, He has His eternal form as a fresh youth. The exact words used in this connection in the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam are vijñānam ajñāna-bhidāpamārjanam. Vijñāna means transcendental knowledge of the Supreme Personality; vijñāna is also experienced knowledge. Transcendental knowledge has to be accepted by the descending process of disciplic succession as Brahmā presents the knowledge of Kṛṣṇa in the Brahma-saṁhitā. Brahma-saṁhitā is vijñāna as realized by Brahmā’s transcendental experience, and in that way he presented the form and the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa in the transcendental abode. Ajñāna-bhidā means “that which can match all kinds of speculation.” In ignorance, people are imagining the form of the Lord; sometimes He has no form and sometimes He has form, according to their different imaginations. But the presentation of Kṛṣṇa in the Brahma-saṁhitā is vijñāna — scientific, experienced knowledge given by Lord Brahmā and accepted by Lord Caitanya. There is no doubt about it. Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s form, Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s flute, Kṛṣṇa’s color — everything is reality. Here it is said that this vijñānam is always defeating all kinds of speculative knowledge. “Therefore,” the demigods prayed, “without Your appearing as Kṛṣṇa, as You are, neither ajñāna-bhidā (the nescience of speculative knowledge) nor vijñānam would be realized. Ajñāna-bhidāpamārjanam — by Your appearance the speculative knowledge of ignorance will be vanquished, and the real, experienced knowledge of authorities like Lord Brahmā will be established. Men influenced by the three modes of material nature imagine their own God according to the modes of material nature. In this way God is presented in various ways, but Your appearance will establish what the real form of God is.” The highest blunder committed by the impersonalist is to think that when the incarnation of God comes, He accepts a form of matter in the mode of goodness. Actually the form of Kṛṣṇa or Nārāyaṇa is transcendental to any material idea. Even the greatest impersonalist, Śaṅkarācārya, has admitted, nārāyaṇaḥ paro ’vyaktāt: the material creation is caused by the avyakta, the impersonal manifestation of matter or the nonphenomenal total reservoir of matter, and Kṛṣṇa is transcendental to that material conception. This is expressed in the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam as śuddha-sattva, or transcendental. The Lord does not belong to the material mode of goodness, for He is above the position of material goodness. He belongs to the transcendental, eternal status of bliss and knowledge. “Dear Lord,” the demigods prayed, “when You appear in Your different incarnations, You take different names and forms according to different situations. Lord Kṛṣṇa is Your name because You are all-attractive; You are called Śyāmasundara because of Your transcendental beauty. Śyāma means blackish, yet they say that You are more beautiful than thousands of cupids. Kandarpa-koṭi-kamanīya . Although You appear in a color which is compared to that of a blackish cloud, You are the transcendental Absolute, and therefore Your beauty is many, many times more attractive than the delicate body of Cupid. Sometimes You are called Giridhārī because You lifted the hill known as Govardhana. You are sometimes called Nanda-nandana or Vāsudeva or Devakī-nandana because You appear as the son of Mahārāja Nanda or Devakī or Vasudeva. Impersonalists think that Your many names or forms are according to a particular type of work and quality because they accept You from the position of a material observer. “Our dear Lord, the way of understanding is not to study Your absolute nature, form and activities by mental speculation. One must engage himself in devotional service; then one can understand Your absolute nature and Your transcendental form, name and quality. Actually, only a person who has a little taste for the service of Your lotus feet can understand Your transcendental nature or form and quality. Others may go on speculating for millions of years, but it is not possible for them to understand even a single part of Your actual position.” In other words, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, cannot be understood by the nondevotees because there is a curtain of yoga-māyā which covers Kṛṣṇa’s actual features. As confirmed in the Bhagavad-gītā (7.25) , nāhaṁ prakāśaḥ sarvasya. The Lord says, “I am not exposed to anyone and everyone.” When Kṛṣṇa came, He was actually present on the Battlefield of Kurukṣetra, and everyone saw Him. But not everyone could understand that He was the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Still, everyone who died in His presence attained complete liberation from material bondage and was transferred to the spiritual world. Because foolish mūḍhas do not awaken their spiritual nature, they do not understand Kṛṣṇa or Rāma ( avajānanti māṁ mūḍhā mānuṣīṁ tanum āśritam ). Even big academic scholars, not considering the endeavors of the ācāryas who have recommended devotional service in many elaborate commentaries and notes, think that Kṛṣṇa is fictitious. This is due to a lack of transcendental knowledge and a failure to awaken Kṛṣṇa consciousness. One should have the common sense to ask why, if Kṛṣṇa or Rāma were fictitious, stalwart scholars like Śrīdhara Svāmī, Rūpa Gosvāmī, Sanātana Gosvāmī, Vīrarāghava, Vijayadhvaja, Vallabhācārya and many other recognized ācāryas would have spent so much time to write about Kṛṣṇa in notes and commentaries on Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    O Lord, cause of all causes, if Your transcendental body were not beyond the modes of material nature, one could not understand the difference between matter and transcendence. Only by Your presence can one understand the transcendental nature of Your Lordship, who are the controller of material nature. Your transcendental nature is very difficult to understand unless one is influenced by the presence of Your transcendental form.
    Commentary

    "Some people try to conclude that my form is material sattva guna." To answer this challenge this verse is spoken. O Lord. This form of yours (idam)-with index finger they point at the womb of Devaki—if it were not, beyond material contamination (nijam sattvam, or suddha sattva), if it were material sattva, then there would be an absence (marjanam apa) of devotees’ realizing your spiritual form (vijnanam). The realization of the devotees is the proof of the Lord’s spiritual form. What do they realize? Because your body is spiritual, by realizing it, material bondage (ajnana) gets extinguished (bhit). One should have no doubt about the reality of their realization. As well there is more evidence of the Lord’s spiritual form. By the strong influence of your qualities, by the appearance of mercy in the form of prema (guna prakasaih which pleases our minds, we can conclude that your body is not material, for those qualities manifest not from matter but from a person possessing spiritual nature. It is you who have those qualities. (yasya ca guna prakasate) . There must be some person to manifest those qualities. Matter alone cannot do that. As well, by the agency strength of suddha sattva (yena va), not by the agency of matter, these qualities must manifest. Another meaning is this: If your suddha sattva body were never to manifest, then realization which destroys ignorance would not take place. If your body were material, then by use of material intelligence (guna prakasaih) you could be inferred. He who possesses matter, and by whose intelligence matter manifests, would be called the Lord.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    O Lord who takes various forms (dhātaḥ)! Your body is inferred by the many functions of intelligence and the senses. The actions of intelligence, related to you, are seen in their relationship to you. For instance, smell has a particular relationship with you, the supreme the witness of all, and intelligence has a similar relationship with you since you as the witness are revealed even in material objects. What is revealed in material things such as a pot is an aspect of the supreme controller. You are the supreme controller. By your power, the jīva also becomes a witness. According to Śrīdhara Svāmī verses 32-34 showed that only the devotee attains liberation. However five verses describe this (32-36). “Why do we need bhakti? The perfection of jṣāna is reached by the absence of guṇas”. But without your sūddha-sattva body, there is no jṣāna. Everything is imaginary only. Śrīdhara Svāmī says that if one serves the Lord’s śuddha-sattva form, one will directly realize the Lord by his mercy. The proofs are many: śreyaḥ-sṛtiṁ bhaktim udasya te vibho kliśyanti ye kevala-bodha-labdhaye teṣām asau kleśala eva śiṣyate nānyad yathā sthūla-tuṣāvaghātinām My dear Lord, devotional service unto you is the best path for self-realization. If someone gives up that path and engages in the cultivation of speculative knowledge, he will simply undergo a troublesome process and will not achieve his desired result. As a person who beats an empty husk of wheat cannot get grain, one who simply speculates cannot achieve self-realization. His only gain is trouble. SB 10.14.4 Gītā says sattvāt saṣjāyate jṣānam: jṣāna arises from sattva. (BG 14.17) Thus jṣāna manifests through material sattva. “Then why accept śuddha-sattva?” The answer is given. O possessor of all śaktis (dhātaḥ)! If this form that we experience is not spiritual (vijṣānam) but material, then it is only a manifestation of jṣāna, even though it is purified by nivikalpa realization, since you are then inferred through the manifestations of material guṇas and not realized. Or, if your spiritual form does not appear on earth, then you will only be inferred through the functions of the senses etc. How? After one realizes Brahman (vijṣānam), that realization is then destroyed (marjanam āpa). With the acceptance of the form of Lord, Brahman realization is cancelled. ātmārāmāś ca munayo nirgranthā apy urukrame kurvanty ahaitukīṁ bhaktim ittham-bhūta-guṇo hariḥ. Some sages who are ātmārāmas, beyond the scriptures, false ego and rules, also practice unmotivated, pure bhakti to the master of pure bhakti, Kṛṣṇa, since he possesses qualities attractive to even them. SB 17.7.10 The method of inference is described. Sattva-guṇa, related to the Lord (yasya), reveals itself as its controller Viṣṇu, just as the dawn indicates the approach o f the sun. By the Lord (yena) sattva-guṇa is manifested, just as smoke is manifested by fire. Because your body is self-manifesting, made of the highest bliss, by its appearance realization of Brahman disappears. Since you have a śakti which reveals your form, that form is not revealed by material sattva. However that form can be inferred just as the sun can be inferred from the dawn. manāṁsy āsan prasannāni sādhūnām asura-druhām When the Lord was about to appear, the saints, who had always been disturbed by demons like Kaṁsa and his men, felt peace within the core of their hearts. SB 10.3.5 sattvādayo na santīśe yatra ca prākṛtā guṇāḥ śuddhaḥ sarva-śuddhebhyaḥ pumān ādyah prasīdatu hlādinī sandhinī samvit tvayy ekā sarva-saṁshite hlāda-tāpakarī miṣrā tvayi no guṇa-varjite May the original person purer than all pure persons, in whom the guṇas of prakṛti such as sattva do not exist, be pleased. Since you are endowed with hlādinī, samvit and sandhinī śaktis, amd are devoid of the material guṇas, you have no mixture of happiness and distress. Or the verse explains the cause of the Lord’s appearance. Without the manifestation of viśuddha-sattva one cannot realize your greatness. If your viśuddha-sattva form, which is your own (nijam), since it is directly related to Svayam Bhagavān, is not manifest, special knowledge of your powers, which destroys ignorance, will not arise (mārjanam āpa). “Since I have appeared as Svayam Bhagavān, what is the question of knowledge?” You are presently inferred only by the manifestations of effulgence in Devakī (guṇa). “But such manifestations are not my unique nature. They are only a manifestation of my expansion.” By these manifestations we infer your qualities. We have not experienced this with Ṣaṅkarṣaṇa’s appearance.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    O Lord who takes various forms (dhātaḥ)! Your body is inferred by the many functions of intelligence and the senses. The word ca means “you who are the shelter of the guṇas.” Or by serving your form, one attains direct bliss. There is no other way. If your body (idam nijam) served out of prema did not exist, then direct realization of you would be destroyed (marjanam āpa). Or destroyer of ignorance! By realization of you, all doubts are destroyed. Or without your avatāra, there could be no knowledge of you as svayam bhagavān, knowledge of bhakti and knowledge of the greatness of devotees (nijam vijṣānam). That knowledge destroys other knowledge, which is ignorance (ajṣāna-bhit). “How do you know that I have appears as an avatāra?” You can be inferred by qualities, like Devakī’s effulgence or my manifestation of qualities in the universe. Tato graha-gaṇaḥ samyak pracacāra divi dvija Viṣṇor aṁśe bhuvaṁ yāte Ṛtavaś cābhavan śubhāḥ The planets wandered freely in the sky. Seasons manifested all beauty when the expansion of Viṣṇu appeared on earth. Viṣṇu Purāṇa “But that happens naturally.” No, belonging to you (yasya) the qualities manifest. By you, the lord, these qualities manifest. Taking sattvam to mean sattva-guṇa, it actually means the best or sāttvikam—things related to you. It is situated in you (nijam). Without these things, there could be no knowledge of you. Without that knowledge what would happen? You could only be inferred by qualities, but not actually known. Or if you were not the form for attaining the highest goal, if you did not appear as an avatāra, could there be knowledge (nijam idam vijṣānam) concerning the greatness of bhakti or our knowledge (nijaṁ vijṣānam)? There could be no realization, because of lack of distinguishing knowledge (ajṣaṇa-bhidā).

    Concepts
    JivaYoga
    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa's form is śuddha-sattva, transcendental to the guṇas — only by His mercy through bhakti, not by speculation, can His real nature be known.
    Practical Applications
    • Refuse to imagine Kṛṣṇa as a product of the material modes — accept His form, name, and pastimes through paramparā as Brahmā presents them in the Brahma-saṁhitā.
    • Spend ten focused minutes today in Deity worship or before His picture, treating Him as personally present, so your transcendental nature is awakened from within.
    • Notice when speculation creeps in — 'maybe God is impersonal,' 'maybe this is symbolic' — and replace it with one verse of bhaktyā mām abhijānāti chanted aloud.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where am I quietly manufacturing my own version of Kṛṣṇa — fitting Him into the mode of nature I happen to be comfortable with — instead of receiving Him as Brahmā and the ācāryas have presented Him?
    • If vijñāna only descends through devotional service and disciplic succession, what speculation am I still trusting more than the words of the ācāryas, and what would it cost me today to reverse that trust?
    For Each Age Group
    youth
    • Notice how much of your sense of who Kṛṣṇa is comes from a feed — reels, memes, aesthetic posts — versus from actually hearing Bhāgavatam read aloud or chanting japa. This week, replace fifteen minutes of scrolling spiritual content with fifteen minutes of hearing a senior devotee read this verse's purport, and watch which one actually changes how you feel by Friday.
    • In your friend group or class, you will be pressured to flatten Kṛṣṇa into 'the universe,' 'energy,' or 'whatever works for you' — it sounds tolerant and costs nothing. Practice once this week saying clearly: 'In my tradition Kṛṣṇa is a person, not a symbol.' Notice the social cost of that sentence. That cost is the modes of nature pushing back; the steadiness you find while saying it is śuddha-sattva pushing forward.
    • Before exams or auditions, you will be tempted to construct a transactional God — 'if I pray, You deliver.' That God is built from your rajas. Try instead: ten minutes of japa with no request attached, just hearing the names. The God who responds to that practice is not the one your anxiety manufactured.
    householder
    • Your children are forming their first image of God right now, and they will form it from whatever has the most repetition and emotional weight in the home — which means your phone, the TV, or the family altar, in that order of current dominance. Decide this week which one wins, and rearrange the evening accordingly: ārati at a fixed time, a Bhāgavatam verse read aloud at dinner, the deity given the visible center of a room.
    • In money and career decisions, you will notice yourself praying to a God shaped by your tax bracket — a God of promotion, of school admissions, of property. That is the guṇa-prakāśa of your own ambition reflected back. Once a week, sit before the deity and offer a decision without asking for an outcome — only asking that your perception of Kṛṣṇa not be reduced to your spreadsheet.
    • Marriage will tempt both partners to remake God in the image of the spouse's preferences — softer, sterner, more permissive, more strict. Read this verse together once a month and ask: are we worshiping Kṛṣṇa as He has revealed Himself through paramparā, or are we negotiating a domestic compromise deity? The honest answer protects the marriage more than the compromise does.
    senior
    • At this stage, the bodies you have already passed through are many, and the next transition is closer than the last one. Use that proximity: each morning, sit before the deity and let the form of Kṛṣṇa — Śyāmasundara, Giridhārī, Nanda-nandana — actually register, not as concept but as the face you intend to see at the moment of leaving. The verse says His form is the only one that is not material; make sure it is the one your mind has rehearsed.
    • Younger family members will ask you, more than you expect, what you actually believe. Resist the senior's temptation to soften it into 'all paths lead to the same place' — that is the impersonalist drift Prabhupāda warns against, and they can sense the evasion. Tell them clearly: Kṛṣṇa is a person, His form is transcendental, and you have spent a lifetime learning to recognize Him. Give them the specific over the safe.
    • Loosen one attachment this month that has quietly become a substitute deity — a property, a grievance, a reputation, a child's career. Offer it formally before the deity and notice that the form of Kṛṣṇa does not flicker when the attachment goes; only your projection of God did. That steadiness is the vijñānam the verse promises — experienced, not speculated.
    Common Pitfalls
    • Treating Kṛṣṇa's transcendental form as a 'symbolic' or 'mode-of-goodness' representation of an impersonal Absolute — the very impersonalist blunder this verse refutes — rather than accepting His form, name, color and flute as śuddha-sattva reality.
    • Trying to 'understand' Kṛṣṇa first through study, debate or mental speculation, and postponing sādhana and Deity worship until the philosophy 'makes sense' — reversing the order the verse insists upon (service first, then realization).
    • Approaching the verse as an intellectual proof of Kṛṣṇa's transcendence while remaining personally untouched — collecting siddhānta as ammunition against impersonalists instead of letting ajñāna-bhidā actually vanquish one's own ignorance and self-manufactured god.
    Discussion Prompts
    • The demigods say Kṛṣṇa's form is śuddha-sattva — beyond even the mode of goodness — yet most of us, when we picture God, picture something we've constructed from our own conditioning. Share with your partner: what is the 'God' you imagine when no one is watching, and how much of that image is actually you projecting upward? Where do you disagree with each other about what counts as 'projection' versus genuine revelation?
    • Prabhupāda is severe in this purport: the impersonalist's 'highest blunder' is to think Kṛṣṇa's form is matter in the mode of goodness. In your group, take the opposite side honestly — argue the case that all forms of God are human constructions shaped by culture. Then have someone respond from the verse. Where does the argument actually break? Where does it feel uncomfortably strong?
    • The verse says only by Kṛṣṇa's presence (guṇa-prakāśaiḥ) can His transcendental nature be inferred. That means scripture, deity, name, and sādhu-saṅga are not optional aids — they are the only access points. Discuss: which of these four do you most neglect, and what speculation has rushed in to fill the vacuum? Be specific with one another, not abstract.
    Role Play

    Two students sit facing each other. Student A is a sincere college friend who says: 'I respect your devotion, but I think Kṛṣṇa is ultimately a beautiful symbol — a personification of the formless Absolute that your tradition uses because human minds need a face. Underneath, we're talking about the same impersonal reality.' Student B must respond as a Gauḍīya practitioner, drawing on SB 10.2.35 — that without Kṛṣṇa's actual transcendental appearance, neither ajñāna-bhidā nor vijñānam can arise; that Śaṅkara himself conceded nārāyaṇaḥ paro 'vyaktāt; and that bhaktyā mām abhijānāti is the only epistemology that works. The teacher pauses the role-play whenever Student B slips into either (a) impersonalist-friendly hedging or (b) defensive aggression, and asks: 'What would a fellow practitioner say here, neither apologizing nor attacking?' Then swap roles.

    Objections & Responses
    • Every culture imagines God in its own image — blue-skinned flute player, old man on a throne, formless light. Saying yours is the 'real' form and the others are 'imagination' is just religious chauvinism dressed up in Sanskrit.
      The verse anticipates exactly this objection. It does not say 'our image is correct and yours is wrong' — it says no image arrived at by speculation, ours included, can reach Him. The point is epistemological, not tribal. Imagined forms arise from the three guṇas and reflect the imaginer's mode — old men, light, abstractions, all of it. The Gauḍīya claim is narrower and stranger: that Kṛṣṇa Himself descends in a form that is not produced by the guṇas but is śuddha-sattva, transcendental to them, and that this form is received through paramparā — Brahmā to Nārada to Vyāsa onward — not invented by it. You can reject that claim, but notice it is not the same claim as 'our culture's picture beats yours.' It is the claim that revelation differs in kind from projection, and that bhakti is the instrument that distinguishes them. Test it with sādhana before rejecting it on grounds it does not actually hold.
    • If Kṛṣṇa is only knowable through devotional service — bhaktyā mām abhijānāti — then this is unfalsifiable. Anyone who doesn't see Him can be told 'you just don't have enough bhakti.' That's a closed circle.
      It would be a closed circle if bhakti were a private feeling. But the tradition specifies bhakti concretely: chanting the holy names a measurable number of times, deity worship at fixed hours, hearing Bhāgavatam under guidance, following the four regulative principles, associating with devotees. This is a method with steps, like any other discipline that produces a perceptual capacity — a musician's ear, a physician's diagnostic eye. Prabhupāda says Deity worship 'even in the absence of the Supreme Personality of Godhead awakens the transcendental nature of the devotee' — meaning the apparatus itself is transformative and testable. The honest response to the verse is not 'this is unfalsifiable' but 'have I actually run the experiment, with the prescribed dosage and duration, under qualified supervision?' Most who raise the objection have not. The circle is open at exactly one point — sādhana — and the verse is inviting you through it.

    O Lord, Your transcendental name and form are not ascertained by those who merely speculate on the path of imagination. Your name, form and attributes can be ascertained only through devotional service.
    Purport

    As stated in the Padma Purāṇa: ataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-nāmādi na bhaved grāhyam indriyaiḥ sevonmukhe hi jihvādau svayam eva sphuraty adaḥ “One cannot understand the transcendental nature of the name, form, quality and pastimes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa through one’s materially contaminated senses. Only when one becomes spiritually saturated by transcendental service to the Lord are the transcendental name, form, quality and pastimes of the Lord revealed to him.” Since Kṛṣṇa and His transcendental name, form and activities are all of a transcendental nature, ordinary persons or those who are only slightly advanced cannot understand them. Even big scholars who are nondevotees think that Kṛṣṇa is fictitious. Yet although so-called scholars and commentators do not believe that Kṛṣṇa was factually a historical person whose presence on the Battlefield of Kurukṣetra is recorded in the history of Mahābhārata, they feel compelled to write commentaries on Bhagavad-gītā and other historical records. Sevonmukhe hi jihvādau svayam eva sphuraty adaḥ: Kṛṣṇa’s transcendental name, form, attributes and activities can be revealed only when one engages in His service in full consciousness. This confirms Kṛṣṇa’s own words in Bhagavad-gītā (18.55) : bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaś cāsmi tattvataḥ tato māṁ tattvato jñātvā viśate tad-anantaram “One can understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead as He is only by devotional service. And when one is in full consciousness of the Supreme Lord by such devotion, he can enter into the kingdom of God.” Only by sevonmukha, by engaging oneself in the Lord’s service, can one realize the name, form and qualities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. “O Lord,” the demigods say, “the impersonalists, who are nondevotees, cannot understand that Your name is identical with Your form.” Since the Lord is absolute, there is no difference between His name and His actual form. In the material world there is a difference between form and name. The mango fruit is different from the name of the mango. One cannot taste the mango fruit simply by chanting, “Mango, mango, mango.” But the devotee who knows that there is no difference between the name and the form of the Lord chants Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare/ Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare, and realizes that he is always in Kṛṣṇa’s company. For persons who are not very advanced in absolute knowledge of the Supreme, Lord Kṛṣṇa exhibits His transcendental pastimes. They can simply think of the pastimes of the Lord and get the full benefit. Since there is no difference between the transcendental name and form of the Lord, there is no difference between the transcendental pastimes and the form of the Lord. For those who are less intelligent (like women, laborers or the mercantile class), the great sage Vyāsadeva wrote Mahābhārata. In the Mahābhārata, Kṛṣṇa is present in His different activities. Mahābhārata is history, and simply by studying, hearing, and memorizing the transcendental activities of Kṛṣṇa, the less intelligent can also gradually rise to the standard of pure devotees. The pure devotees, who are always absorbed in the thought of the transcendental lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa and who are always engaged in devotional service in full Kṛṣṇa consciousness, are never to be considered to be in the material world. Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī has explained that those who are always engaged in Kṛṣṇa consciousness by body, mind and activities are to be considered liberated even within this body. This is also confirmed in the Bhagavad-gītā: those who are engaged in the devotional service of the Lord have already transcended the material position. Kṛṣṇa appears in order to give a chance to both the devotees and the nondevotees for realization of the ultimate goal of life. The devotees get the direct chance to see Him and worship Him. Those who are not on that platform get the chance to become acquainted with His activities and thus become elevated to the same position. The Brahma-saṁhitā (5.38) says: premāñjana-cchurita-bhakti-vilocanena santaḥ sadaiva hṛdayeṣu vilokayanti yaṁ śyāmasundaram acintya-guṇa-svarūpaṁ govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi Although Kṛṣṇa’s transcendental form is presented as black, devotees who are in love with the Supreme Personality of Godhead appreciate the Lord as Śyāmasundara, having a very beautiful blackish form. The Lord’s form is so beautiful that the Brahma-saṁhitā (5.30) also states: veṇuṁ kvaṇantam aravinda-dalāyatākṣaṁ barhāvataṁsam asitāmbuda-sundarāṅgam kandarpa-koṭi-kamanīya-viśeṣa-śobhaṁ govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi “I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, who plays on His transcendental flute. His eyes are like lotus flowers, He is decorated with peacock plumes, and His bodily color resembles the color of a fresh black cloud, although His bodily features are more beautiful than millions of Cupids.” This beauty of the Supreme Lord can be seen by devotees who are in love with Him, devotees whose eyes are anointed with love of Godhead ( premāñjana-cchurita-bhakti-vilocanena ). The Lord is also known as Giridhārī or Girivara-dhārī. Because Kṛṣṇa, for the sake of His devotees, lifted Govardhana Hill, the devotees appreciate the Lord’s inconceivable strength; but nondevotees, in spite of directly perceiving the Lord’s inconceivable strength and power, regard the Lord’s activities as fictitious. This is the difference between a devotee and a nondevotee. Nondevotees cannot give any nomenclature for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, yet the Lord is known as Śyāmasundara and Giridhārī. Similarly, the Lord is known as Devakī-nandana and Yaśodā-nandana because He accepted the role of son for mother Devakī and mother Yaśodā, and He is known as Gopāla because He enjoyed the sport of maintaining the cows and calves. Therefore, although He has no mundane name, He is addressed by devotees as Devakī-nandana, Yaśodā-nandana, Gopāla and Śyāmasundara. These are all transcendental names that only devotees can appreciate and nondevotees cannot. The history of Kṛṣṇa the person has been openly seen by everyone, yet only those who are in love with the Supreme Personality of Godhead can appreciate this history, whereas nondevotees, who have not developed their loving qualities, think that the activities, form and attributes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead are fictitious. Therefore this verse explains, na nāma-rūpe guṇa janma-karmabhir nirūpitavye tava tasya sākṣiṇaḥ. In this connection, Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura has given the example that persons suffering from jaundice cannot taste the sweetness of sugar candy, although everyone knows that sugar candy is sweet. Similarly, because of the material disease, nondevotees cannot understand the transcendental name, form, attributes and activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, although they actually see the Lord’s activities, either through authority or through history. The Purāṇas are old, authentic histories, but nondevotees cannot understand them, especially Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, which is the essence of Vedic knowledge. Nondevotees cannot understand even the preliminary study of transcendental knowledge, Bhagavad-gītā. They simply speculate and present commentaries with absurd distortions. In conclusion, unless one elevates himself to the transcendental platform by practicing bhakti-yoga, one cannot understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead or His name, form, attributes or activities. But if by chance, by the association of devotees, one can actually understand the Lord and His features, one immediately becomes a liberated person. As the Lord says in Bhagavad-gītā (4.9) : janma karma ca me divyam evaṁ yo vetti tattvataḥ tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma naiti mām eti so ’rjuna “One who knows the transcendental nature of My appearance and activities does not, upon leaving the body, take his birth again in this material world, but attains My eternal abode, O Arjuna.” Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī has therefore said that by affection and love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, devotees can express their mind to Him with their words. Others, however, cannot do this, as confirmed in Bhagavad-gītā ( bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaś cāsmi tattvataḥ ).

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    O Lord, Your transcendental name and form are not ascertained by those who merely speculate on the path of imagination. Your name, form and attributes can be ascertained only through devotional service.
    Commentary

    Not only your form is suddha sattva, but also your name. Both name and form can be realized only by devotion. There is no other way. Thus this verse is spoken. Guna here refers to His beautiful form and merciful glance. Karma refers to lifting Govardhana hill, skillfully posing with three bends etc. Janma refers to his role as son of Nanda and Vasudeva . The witnessing jiva cannot discern or realize your sweetness, with your qualities, activities and birth, through chanting your name or meditating on your form. Not realizing the sweetness of your name or form,is no realization at all. It is like those afflicted with jaundice: though they chew sugar candy, they cannot taste the sweetness. As those devoid of devotion cannot realize the sweetness of your name and form, your name and form must also be suddha sattva, purely spiritual. Saksinah can also refer to the supreme Lord, the Supreme witness. Because your name and form are part of your spiritual nature, those pursuing the path of speculation cannot know your true form. However, for the person who has attained prema bhakti (vartamah), engages in service such as hearing and chanting your names with devotion (kriyayam) the name and form of the Lord can be directly realized. This can be inferred through mind (mental attitudes such as tolerance, pridelessness) and words (steeped in devotion) of the devotee.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    “Name and form are conceptions in the mind. Why do you describe my form in this way?” This verse answers. Your name and form along with your qualities, birth and activities, cannot be realized as they truly are. An example of a name expressing qualities is Bhakta-vatsala. A name expressing his form is Śyāmasundara. A name expressing his actions is Govardhanodharaṇa. A form expressing his actions is Venuvadana or Tribhaṅga-lalita. A name expressing his birth is Devakī-nandana and a form expressing his birth is Matsya. Or your name and form cannot be realized by studying of scriptures (guṇa), by following proper conduct or yamas and niyamas (karma), or by birth in a brāhmaṇa family (janma). You cannot be realized because one can only infer about you by logic and words of scripture and not experience your name and form through these means. The reason is given. You are the direct witness (sakṣiṇaḥ) of the intelligence etc. Your sweet qualities cannot be realized by the material senses and intelligence. The cause and effect are as if moving in opposite directions. By being related to the witness your name and form have similar qualities. However you can be realized by the wise since they are also filled with the highest bliss. tad aśma-sāraṁ hṛdayaṁ batedaṁ yad gṛhyamāṇair hari-nāma-dheyaiḥ | na vikriyetātha yadā vikāro netre jalaṁ gātra-ruheṣu harṣaḥ || That heart which does not transform on hearing the names of the Lord, even though he shows tears in the eyes and hair standing on end, is made of iron. SB 2.3.24 rūpaṁ yad etad avabodha-rasodayena śaśvan-nivṛtta-tamasaḥ sad-anugrahāya ādau gṛhītam avatāra-śataika-bījaṁ yan-nābhi-padma-bhavanād aham āvirāsam The form which I see is eternally freed from material contamination and has appeared in this world to show mercy to the devotees as a manifestation of internal potency. This incarnation is the origin of many other incarnations, and I am born from the lotus flower grown from your navel home. SB 3.9.2 nātaḥ paraṁ parama yad bhavataḥ svarūpam ānanda-mātram avikalpam aviddha-varcaḥ paśyāmi viśva-sṛjam ekam aviśvam ātman bhūtendriyātmaka-madas ta upāśrito ’smi O Supreme Lord! I do not see that you are different from your form as the Brahman which is without qualities and only bliss. O form of unrestricted light! I, full of pride in thinking I can get pleasure by body, sense and mind, take shelter of your one form which is spiritual, but which creates this universe. SB 3.9.3 People can realize your name and form as they are in truth (pratīyanti) through actions (kriyāyām) like singing your name or meditating on your form. bhaktyāham ekayā grāhyaḥ śraddhayātmā priyaḥ satām bhaktiḥ punāti man-niṣṭhā śva-pākān api sambhavāt Only by bhakti with full faith can the devotees obtain me, Paramātmā, the object of love. Bhakti fixed in me purifies even a dog eater of his low birth. SB 11.14.21 Śrīdhara Svāmī interprets the verse as follows. Your spiritual forms worshipped by weak forms of remembrance cannot be realized since the forms are beyond words and mind. Form and name, aspects of your tattva, belong to the witness of everything, and are thus beyond words and mind. You can be directly seen by worship, using the mind and other methods of worship which employ the external senses.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Your name and form along with your qualities, birth and activities, cannot be realized as they truly are. An example of a name expressing qualities is Bhakta-vatsala. A name expressing his form is Śyāmasundara. A name expressing his actions is Govardhanadhāri. A form expressing his actions is Venuvadana or Tribhaṅga-lalita. A name expressing his birth is Devakī-nandana and a form expressing his birth is Matsya (born in water). Or your name and form cannot be realized by studying of scriptures (guṇa), by following proper conduct or yamas and niyamas (karma), or by birth in a brāhmaṇa family (janma). They realize and develop faith in (pratiyanti) the greatness of your name and form by worship. Or they realize your or the name and form by worship. You can be inferred by words and mind, but not attained since you are the witness of words and mind (tasya). You are the witness of names and forms also. But those who perform worship (kriyāyām) realize you, since the name and named, and form and possessor of the form are non-different. Or not being defined by name and form, by mercy you have appear as an avatāra (tava). Or having glorified the Lord’s form, the name is glorified. The two are glorified together, referring to the nature of the form previously described. Let name and form not be defined since they are beyond the guṇas and yet have qualities. “One object having qualities and not having qualities is impossible.” True, but those who perform worship can understand this, and not others.

    Concepts
    JivaYoga
    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa's name, form, and pastimes are not unlocked by speculation — they reveal themselves only to a tongue and life engaged in His service.
    Practical Applications
    • Chant a fixed number of Hare Kṛṣṇa rounds today on beads, treating the holy name as non-different from Kṛṣṇa Himself rather than as a mantra-technique.
    • Refuse to settle any question about Kṛṣṇa today by mental speculation — instead, render one concrete service (cook an offering, clean the altar, read aloud from Bhāgavatam) and let understanding follow.
    • Notice when you reduce Kṛṣṇa to 'the divine within' or 'consciousness,' and re-address Him by a personal name from the verse — Devakī-nandana, Yaśodā-nandana, Gopāla, Śyāmasundara.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where in my study of Kṛṣṇa am I still relying on intellectual speculation and 'mental imagination' rather than the sevonmukha attitude this verse insists is the only door?
    • Like the jaundiced person who cannot taste sugar candy, what specific 'material disease' in me right now is dulling my taste for Kṛṣṇa's name, form and pastimes — and what service could begin to cure it?
    For Each Age Group
    youth
    • Notice this week how often you try to *understand* Kṛṣṇa or your tradition in order to *defend* it to skeptical friends or in a class discussion. Each time, redirect: instead of one more argument, do one small act of sevā — chant a round, clean the altar, cook something to offer. Watch whether your clarity in conversation actually improves on the days you serve more.
    • Pick one social-media account you follow that fuels speculative spirituality (manifesting, 'the universe,' impersonal 'energy,' generic mindfulness). Unfollow it for a week. In that space, listen to one Bhāgavatam class on Kṛṣṇa's pastimes. Notice the difference between content that flatters your ahaṅkāra and content that asks you to bow.
    • When you study for exams, you accept that you cannot understand calculus by 'feeling' it — you have to do problems. Apply the same to bhakti. Set a non-negotiable daily japa minimum (start with four rounds if sixteen feels impossible) and treat it as the laboratory work of this verse. Skip the philosophical debate until you have done the practice.
    householder
    • Your children are watching whether Kṛṣṇa is real to you — not in your words, but in your hands. This week, let them see you offer the food before anyone eats, let them hear you chant while you drive them to school. The verse says the form is revealed through service; your home is the laboratory.
    • When a financial decision comes up — a job change, a purchase, a school for the children — notice how quickly you reach for spreadsheets and projections (the speculative path the verse warns against). Before the analysis, sit for ten minutes in front of the deity or a picture of Kṛṣṇa and offer the decision. Then do the spreadsheet. The spreadsheet is not wrong; the order matters.
    • With your spouse, identify one shared act of sevā this month — cooking for a Sunday program, sponsoring a class, hosting a kīrtana at home. Marriage in the gṛhastha-āśrama is not just shared logistics; it is shared service. The verse promises that Kṛṣṇa's form becomes real to those who serve. Test it together.
    senior
    • You have spent decades accumulating the data of a life — careers, opinions, accomplishments, grievances. The verse says none of that data has touched Kṛṣṇa's actual nāma-rūpa. Take one hour this week to sit with that humbling fact, and let the chanting become primary, the résumé secondary. The jaundice the purport names is the disease of accumulated viṣaya; vairāgya is the cure that comes through sevā, not through retirement.
    • When you mentor younger devotees or family members, resist the urge to teach Kṛṣṇa philosophically — you have read the books, you know the arguments. Instead, tell them the pastimes. Govardhana, Dāmodara, the rāsa-līlā as Prabhupāda presents it. The verse and purport say the pastimes themselves carry the Lord. Be a story-bearer, not a debater, in this stage.
    • Mortality is closing the gap between what you know intellectually and what you have realized through service. Each evening, name aloud one bodily attachment you are willing to loosen — a possession, a role, a self-image — and offer it at Kṛṣṇa's feet. The verse promises that as the speculative grip releases, the form of Śyāmasundara, Yaśodā-nandana, Giridhārī becomes vivid to the devotee whose eyes are anointed with prema.
    Common Pitfalls
    • Treating 'devotional service reveals the Lord' as a passive waiting game — assuming realization will arrive on its own, without actually engaging tongue, ears and hands in concrete sevā today.
    • Reading the verse as a license for anti-intellectualism — dismissing scriptural study (svādhyāya) and careful hearing, when in fact the verse criticizes speculation divorced from service, not disciplined study under devotees.
    • Quietly conceding the impersonalist premise — agreeing that Kṛṣṇa's name, form and pastimes are 'symbolic' or 'metaphorical' for non-devotees, instead of holding firmly that name and form are non-different and historically real, and that the limitation lies in the perceiver, not in Him.
    Discussion Prompts
    • The verse insists Kṛṣṇa's name, form, and qualities are revealed only through sevā — not through study, debate, or speculation. Share with your partner one area of your spiritual life where you have been trying to *think* your way to Kṛṣṇa instead of *serve* your way to Him. Where do you disagree with the verse's claim that intellect alone cannot reach Him?
    • Prabhupāda compares the nondevotee scholar to a jaundiced patient who cannot taste sugar candy. Discuss in your group: is this fair to the sincere academic, the philosophical seeker, the comparative-religion student? When does the jaundice metaphor cut you personally, and when does it feel like it lets devotees off the hook from rigorous thinking?
    • The purport says Mahābhārata was given for 'the less intelligent' — women, laborers, the mercantile class. Sit with the discomfort of that line. Does the verse's deeper teaching (that pastimes themselves are non-different from the Lord) rescue this, or does it still trouble you? Where in your own life are you the 'less intelligent' one who needs story rather than philosophy?
    Role Play

    Two students. Student A is a devotee for five years, chants sixteen rounds, reads daily. Student B is A's college roommate, a sharp philosophy major who has just read the Gītā in a comparative-religion seminar and tells A over dinner: 'Look, I've read your book. Kṛṣṇa is a beautiful literary figure, like Achilles. Your guru's commentary is sectarian. The text itself supports an impersonal reading — Brahman, the Self, consciousness. You're projecting a personal God onto an abstract truth.' A must respond from SB 10.2.36 — without quoting the verse academically, without becoming defensive, and without conceding the impersonalist reading. The teacher pauses the scene every two minutes and asks the class: did A serve Kṛṣṇa in that exchange, or defend Him? What is the difference?

    Objections & Responses
    • This verse is circular and unfalsifiable. You say Kṛṣṇa can only be known through devotion — so any nondevotee who disagrees is dismissed by definition as 'jaundiced.' That's not an argument; it's an immunization against criticism. Every cult uses the same move.
      The circularity is real, and the verse owns it openly — that is its honesty, not its evasion. Every domain of knowledge has an entry condition: you cannot taste sweetness without a tongue, cannot hear music without an ear, cannot do mathematics without first accepting axioms you did not derive. Bhakti is the organ for perceiving Kṛṣṇa, just as the eye is the organ for perceiving color. The verse does not say 'reject all critique'; it says the instrument matters. Test it as you would any instrument — engage in sevā for a measured period, chant the names with attention, and observe what shifts in your perception. The Padma Purāṇa cited in the purport — sevonmukhe hi jihvādau svayam eva sphuraty adaḥ — is not a demand for blind faith but an invitation to a specific experiment. The cult uses the same move only verbally; it does not offer a method that anyone, of any background, can run and verify in their own consciousness.
    • If Kṛṣṇa's name and form can only be grasped by devotees, then the whole missionary project of the movement is incoherent. Why preach to nondevotees at all? Why translate Bhagavad-gītā for the public if they are constitutionally unable to understand it?
      The purport itself answers this — read it again. Prabhupāda says Kṛṣṇa appears 'to give a chance to both the devotees and the nondevotees for realization of the ultimate goal of life.' The nondevotee cannot grasp the tattva immediately, but he can hear the pastimes, study the activities, and 'gradually rise to the standard of pure devotees.' That is exactly why Vyāsa wrote Mahābhārata. The translation, the book distribution, the public class — these are not claims that the reader will understand on first contact. They are seed-planting. The verse rules out *speculation* as a path, not *hearing* (śravaṇam). Hearing Kṛṣṇa's name and pastimes from a devotee — even with no prior faith — is itself the beginning of sevā. Preaching is not a contradiction of the verse; it is its practical extension.

    Even while engaged in various activities, devotees whose minds are completely absorbed at Your lotus feet, and who constantly hear, chant, contemplate and cause others to remember Your transcendental names and forms, are always on the transcendental platform, and thus they can understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
    Purport

    How bhakti-yoga can be practiced is explained in this verse. Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī has said that anyone who has dedicated his life to the service of the Lord ( īhā yasya harer dāsye ) by his activities, his mind and his words ( karmaṇā manasā girā ) may stay in any condition of life ( nikhilāsv apy avasthāsu ) and yet is no longer actually conditioned but is liberated ( jīvan-muktaḥ sa ucyate ). Even though such a devotee is in a material body, he has nothing to do with this body, for he is transcendentally situated. Nārāyaṇa-parāḥ sarve na kutaścana bibhyati: because a devotee is engaged in transcendental activities, he is not afraid of being materially embodied. ( Bhāg. 6.17.28 ) Illustrating this liberated position, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu prayed, mama janmani janmanīśvare bhavatād bhaktir ahaitukī tvayi: “All I want is Your causeless devotional service in My life, birth after birth.” Even if a devotee, by the supreme will of the Lord, takes birth in this material world, he continues his devotional service. When King Bharata made a mistake and in his next life became a deer, his devotional service did not stop, although some slight chastisement was given to him because of his negligence. Nārada Muni says that even if one falls from the platform of devotional service, he is not lost, whereas nondevotees are lost entirely because they are not engaged in service. Bhagavad-gītā (9.14) therefore recommends that one always engage at least in chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra: satataṁ kīrtayanto māṁ yatantaś ca dṛḍha-vratāḥ namasyantaś ca māṁ bhaktyā nitya-yuktā upāsate “Always chanting My glories, endeavoring with great determination, bowing down before Me, the great souls perpetually worship Me with devotion.” One should not give up the process of devotional service, which is performed in nine different ways ( śravaṇaṁ kīrtanaṁ viṣṇoḥ smaraṇaṁ pāda-sevanam, etc.). The most important process is hearing ( śravaṇam ) from the guru, sādhu and śāstra — the spiritual master, the saintly ācāryas and the Vedic literature. Sādhu-śāstra-guru-vākya, cittete kariyā aikya . We should not hear the commentaries and explanations of nondevotees, for this is strictly forbidden by Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī, who quotes from the Padma Purāṇa: avaiṣṇava-mukhodgīrṇaṁ pūtaṁ hari-kathāmṛtam śravaṇaṁ naiva kartavyaṁ sarpocchiṣṭaṁ yathā payaḥ We should strictly follow this injunction and never try to hear from Māyāvādīs, impersonalists, voidists, politicians or so-called scholars. Strictly avoiding such inauspicious association, we should simply hear from pure devotees. Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī therefore recommends, śrī-guru-padāśrayaḥ: one must seek shelter at the lotus feet of a pure devotee who can be one’s guru. Caitanya Mahāprabhu advises that a guru is one who strictly follows the instructions of Bhagavad-gītā: yare dekha tare kaha ‘kṛṣṇa’-upadeśa (Cc. Madhya 7.128). A juggler, a magician or one who speaks nonsense as an academic career is not a guru. Rather, a guru is one who presents Bhagavad-gītā, Kṛṣṇa’s instructions, as it is. Śravaṇa is very important; one must hear from the Vaiṣṇava sādhu, guru and śāstra. The word kriyāsu, meaning “by manual labor” or “by work,” is important in this verse. One should engage in practical service to the Lord. In our Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, all our activities are concentrated upon distributing Kṛṣṇa literature. This is very important. One may approach any person and induce him to read Kṛṣṇa literature so that in the future he also may become a devotee. Such activities are recommended in this verse. Kriyāsu yas tvac-caraṇāravindayoḥ . Such activities will always remind the devotees of the Lord’s lotus feet. By fully concentrating on distributing books for Kṛṣṇa, one is fully absorbed in Kṛṣṇa. This is samādhi.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Even while engaged in various activities, devotees whose minds are completely absorbed at Your lotus feet, and who constantly hear, chant, contemplate and cause others to remember Your transcendental names and forms, are always on the transcendental platform, and thus they can understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
    Commentary

    This verse points out that practice of hearing, glorifying and remembering the name and form of the Lord is the means for realization of the Lord. The word kriyasu indicates that even in the midst of matters relating to ones material body, the devotee is not affected by the material world, but remains deeply absorbed in the happiness of his realization of the Lord.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    “If these actions are the cause of realization, why do they not produce realization from the beginning?” There are impressions of material addiction, nāma aparādhas, which act as obstacles. But these disappear by constant practice of the actions. That is explained in this verse. Varieties in each of the processes should be understood. The names and forms are considered auspicious (maṅgalāni) because they destroy all suffering and produce the highest bliss. Thus the processes are by their nature the highest goal. One who is situated in his unlimited duties, by becoming absorbed in your lotus feet, goes beyond samṣāra. Or, the person who hears, chants and remembers your auspicious names and forms, becoming absorbed in these devotional acts at your lotus feet, or becomes absorbed in your pastimes, is beyond saṁsāra. Instead of yas tvac sometimes yuṣmad (your) is seen. This person is beyond saṁsāra. Though saṁsāra exists, he is not affected by it. He has no desire for it.

    Concepts
    JivaYoga
    Personal Guidance
    Hear, chant, remember, and help others remember Kṛṣṇa's names and forms — even mid-task, a mind fixed at His lotus feet stays transcendental.
    Practical Applications
    • Begin one ordinary task today (cooking, commuting, emailing) by audibly chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, and keep returning the mind to His lotus feet whenever it drifts.
    • Hear hari-kathā only from a bona fide Vaiṣṇava sādhu, guru, or śāstra today — refuse podcasts, commentaries, or videos by Māyāvādīs, impersonalists, or so-called scholars.
    • Engage in kriyā — concrete service — by handing one piece of Kṛṣṇa literature to someone, or reading aloud from Bhāgavatam to a family member, so others too remember His names.
    Reflection Questions
    • Across the activities that fill my day — work, errands, meals, conversations — where does my consciousness actually rest, and what would it take to relocate it at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet without abandoning the activity itself?
    • Which sources am I currently allowing to shape my hearing about Kṛṣṇa — guru, sādhu, śāstra, or the commentaries of non-devotees, impersonalists, and so-called scholars — and what specifically must I stop ingesting to protect my śravaṇa?
    For Each Age Group
    youth
    • Audit your feed for one week. Every account, podcast, and 'spiritual influencer' you consume — ask: would Sanātana Gosvāmī call this milk, or milk touched by the serpent? Unfollow at least three sources that fail the test, even ones your friends quote.
    • During exam prep or a long study session, set a quiet rule: every time you switch tabs or take a break, chant one round of Hare Kṛṣṇa before scrolling. Make the kriyā of studying itself the place where smaraṇam lives, instead of waiting for a 'free' moment that never comes.
    • Instead of debating Kṛṣṇa consciousness with skeptical friends, give one of them a book — physically, in their hand. Prabhupāda calls book distribution samādhi. Your hostel room or college campus is the field; one book given with sincerity outranks an hour of clever argument.
    householder
    • Pick one weekly family activity — cooking, the school commute, paying bills — and convert it explicitly into a kriyā at His lotus feet: chant aloud during it, or discuss one line of śāstra with your spouse or child while doing it. Stop pretending sādhana lives only on the cushion at 5 a.m.
    • Examine where your family's money and time go for 'spiritual content' — courses, retreats, books, streaming teachers. Apply the avaiṣṇava-mukhodgīrṇa test rigorously and redirect that budget toward guru, sādhu, and śāstra in the paramparā. Your children are watching what you actually fund.
    • Take on one concrete book-distribution commitment as a household — even one book a month, given to a neighbor, a colleague, a relative. Let your children see you do it. This is the kriyā Prabhupāda places at the center; do not outsource it to the temple.
    senior
    • Reorganize your daily routine so that the activities still in your hands — walking, cooking for grandchildren, phone calls, doctor visits — become explicit kriyās of smaraṇam and saṅkīrtanam. The body is narrowing its options; let bhakti expand into every remaining one.
    • Mentor a younger devotee in śravaṇam from guru, sādhu, śāstra. Your legacy is not your savings or your stories; it is whether you transmitted the discipline of hearing only from pure sources. Sit with one person weekly and read Prabhupāda's purports aloud together.
    • Meditate daily on Caitanya Mahāprabhu's prayer quoted in the purport — mama janmani janmanīśvare bhavatād bhaktir ahaitukī tvayi. As mortality comes closer, loosen the grip on 'finishing well' in worldly terms and ask only for uninterrupted devotional service, birth after birth.
    Common Pitfalls
    • Treating 'absorption at the lotus feet' as an internal mood that excuses withdrawal from kriyā — practical service, manual labor, book distribution — when the verse explicitly unites the two.
    • Assuming that any 'spiritual' input qualifies as śravaṇa, and casually consuming Māyāvādī, impersonalist, or academic commentaries on the same texts, ignoring Sanātana Gosvāmī's warning that this is milk touched by a serpent's lips.
    • Reducing the four practices — śṛṇvan, gṛṇan, saṁsmarayan, cintayan — to private hearing and chanting alone, while neglecting saṁsmarayan (causing others to remember) by failing to share Kṛṣṇa-kathā or Kṛṣṇa literature with the people one meets.
    Discussion Prompts
    • The verse promises that even in the middle of ordinary kriyās, a devotee absorbed at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet remains transcendental. Share with your partner one specific activity from your week where you tried this — and one where it felt impossible or even fake. Where is the line between genuine absorption and self-deception?
    • Prabhupāda is uncompromising: do not hear hari-kathā from Māyāvādīs, impersonalists, voidists, politicians, or so-called scholars. In an age of podcasts, YouTube ācāryas, and 'spiritual but not religious' commentators, name one source you currently consume that would fail this test — and argue, honestly, whether you are willing to drop it.
    • Prabhupāda equates book distribution with samādhi and calls it the central kriyā of the movement. Do you actually believe distributing Kṛṣṇa literature is equivalent to deep meditation, or does that sound like sectarian inflation? Push back, and let your partner defend the verse.
    Role Play

    Two students, A and B. A is a serious devotee working a demanding corporate job. B is A's close friend and colleague — sympathetic, intellectually curious, but firmly secular, and a fan of a popular non-devotee 'Gītā teacher' on YouTube whose talks frame Kṛṣṇa as a metaphor for inner consciousness. Over lunch, B says: 'I started listening to him because of you. You should hear his episode on SB 10.2.37 — he says the whole verse is about mindfulness at work.' A must respond in real time, honoring the friendship, without flinching from Sanātana Gosvāmī's injunction (sarpocchiṣṭaṁ yathā payaḥ) and without becoming preachy or dismissive. After 4–5 minutes, swap roles. Then debrief as a group: where did A soften the teaching to keep the friendship? Where did A become harsh and lose the friend? What would actually be śravaṇam from a sādhu in that moment?

    Objections & Responses
    • This sounds like spiritual bypassing. 'Stay absorbed in Kṛṣṇa while you do anything' becomes a license to keep living a materialistic life and just slap a mental label of 'devotion' on top. How is this different from telling someone to think about God while they keep chasing money, status, and sense gratification?
      The verse is precise about what the absorption is in — tvac-caraṇāravindayoḥ, Your lotus feet — and Prabhupāda is precise about what the kriyās are: śravaṇam, kīrtanam, smaraṇam, and concretely, distributing Kṛṣṇa literature. He does not say 'do anything you like and think of Kṛṣṇa.' He says engage your karmaṇā manasā girā in His service. Bypassing happens when we keep viṣaya untouched and add a Kṛṣṇa-flavored mood; bhakti happens when the activity itself is reorganized around Him. The test is simple: is the activity something you could honestly offer? If not, it is not what the verse is describing.
    • Prabhupāda's hard line — never hear from Māyāvādīs, impersonalists, scholars, politicians — feels like intellectual quarantine. In a pluralist world, refusing to listen to anyone outside the lineage looks like fundamentalism, not devotion.
      Sanātana Gosvāmī's image is not fundamentalism, it is hygiene: milk touched by serpent's lips is still milk, but it now carries poison. The objection assumes the content is neutral and only the source varies; the Gauḍīya position is that hari-kathā transmits the bhāva of the speaker, not just information. A scholar who treats Kṛṣṇa as mythology cannot transmit śraddhā in Him, however eloquent. This is not a refusal to think; it is a refusal to let the most precious organ — śravaṇa — be shaped by those who do not accept what is being heard. We can read widely for many purposes; for the food of the soul, we choose the cook carefully.

    O Lord, we are fortunate because the heavy burden of the demons upon this earth is immediately removed by Your appearance. Indeed, we are certainly fortunate, for we shall be able to see upon this earth and in the heavenly planets the marks of lotus, conchshell, club and disc that adorn Your lotus feet.
    Purport

    The soles of the Lord’s lotus feet are marked with śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-padma — conchshell, disc, club and lotus — and also by a flag and a thunderbolt. When Kṛṣṇa walks on this earth or in the heavenly planets, these marks are visible wherever He goes. Vṛndāvana-dhāma is a transcendental place because of Kṛṣṇa’s walking on this land frequently. The inhabitants of Vṛndāvana were fortunate to see these marks here and there. When Akrūra went to Vṛndāvana to take Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma away to the festival arranged by Kaṁsa, upon seeing the marks of the Lord’s lotus feet on the ground of Vṛndāvana, he fell down and began to groan. These marks are visible to devotees who receive the causeless mercy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead ( tavānukampitām ). The demigods were jubilant not only because the appearance of the Supreme Lord would do away with the burdensome demons, but also because they would be able to see upon the ground the transcendental marks from the soles of the Lord’s lotus feet. The gopīs always thought of the Lord’s lotus feet when He was walking in the pasturing grounds, and, as described in the previous verse, simply by thinking of the Lord’s lotus feet, the gopīs were fully absorbed in transcendence ( āviṣṭa-cetā na bhavāya kalpate ). Like the gopīs, one who is always absorbed in thought of the Lord is beyond the material platform and will not remain in this material world. It is our duty, therefore, always to hear, chant and think about the Lord’s lotus feet, as actually done by Vaiṣṇavas who have decided to live in Vṛndāvana always and think of the Lord’s lotus feet twenty-four hours a day.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    O Lord, we are fortunate because the heavy burden of the demons upon this earth is immediately removed by Your appearance. Indeed, we are certainly fortunate, for we shall be able to see upon this earth and in the heavenly planets the marks of lotus, conchshell, club and disc that adorn Your lotus feet.
    Commentary

    In this verse the devatas hint at the Lord’s purpose of relieving the earth’s burden. Pada here means "coming from the feet," as the sruti says, "Padbhyam bhumi" the earth arose from the Lord’s feet. The burden of the earth, which arose from your feet, has been removed. We have understood that Kamsa, Jarsandha and others have been killed just by your appearance. We are fortunate to see the earth (gam) and heaven (dyam) mercifully marked with your young feet (padakaih), marked with flag and thunderbolt (susobhanaih).

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    It is our good fortune that you have relieved the earth (which are your feet) of suffering by your appearance. Or by attaining the highest fortune of your feet when you appear, you have relieved the earth of suffering. Actually the meaning should be “You have relieved the earth which arises from your feet.” But because cause and effect are non-different, the expression padaḥ bhuvaḥ (the burden of the earth which is your foot) is used. Śruti says padyām bhūmiḥ: earth arises from your feet. Akrūra later says agnir mukhaṁ te ’vanir aṅghriḥ: your face is fire and your feet are the earth. (SB 10.40.13) You have removed the suffering caused by Kaṁsa (bhāraḥ) by your appearance in Devakī (janmanā). Because of this, they say “O Lord who removes suffering (hare)!” One goal has been accomplished by benefiting the earth and devotees like us by removing the suffering of the earth which becomes the receptacle of the fragrance of your feet. But the main goal which gives success to all people will be accomplished by your astounding pastimes which give the earth and us the highest benefit. By good fortune we will see the earth marked with your little feet (padakaiḥ). The Lord should actually appear at the end of Dvārakā with a huge body like the devatās. But by mercy he appears with a small, soft body. The earth is ornamented with his foot prints and the heavens receive his mercy by his killing demons. Or the earth get s his foot prints and also his mercy by his foot prints or by spreading of bhakti, and the heavens get his mercy and his footprints when he takes the pārijāta tree since he left footprints in the pollen which fell from the pārijāta.

    Concepts
    Jiva
    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, marked with śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-padma, sanctify every place He walks — devotees who receive His mercy see and live in those marks.
    Practical Applications
    • Begin your morning by mentally tracing the śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-padma marks of Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, then carry that image into your first task.
    • Refuse to treat your workplace or home as ordinary ground — speak and act as if Kṛṣṇa's footprints could appear there, because for a devotee they do.
    • Each evening, name one 'burden of demons' (anger, envy, lust) Kṛṣṇa removed from you today, and thank Him aloud before sleep.
    Reflection Questions
    • The demigods rejoiced not only that the burden of demons would be lifted, but that they would now see Kṛṣṇa's footprints on the earth — where in my own life am I more eager for relief from problems than for the actual darśana of the Lord's presence?
    • Akrūra fell down and groaned upon seeing the marks of the lotus feet on Vṛndāvana's soil — what would it take for me to develop that quality of vision, where ordinary ground becomes sacred because He has walked there?
    For Each Age Group
    youth
    • When you scroll your feed today, notice that you are training your eyes to see brand logos, follower counts, and aesthetic 'marks' everywhere — practice instead remembering, even for thirty seconds before you open the app, that Kṛṣṇa's śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-padma are the marks worth being trained to see.
    • Before your next exam or audition, instead of the usual 'please let me get the result I want,' offer the effort at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet the way the demigods offered their gratitude — concretely, out loud, in your own words — and notice how much of your anxiety was actually about controlling the fruit.
    • Pick one friend group or online space where you have been quietly tolerating an asuric tone (cruelty dressed as humor, contempt dressed as honesty) — and recognize that your private relief when an adult or moderator finally intervenes is a small echo of what the demigods feel in this verse; then ask whether your own sva-dharma in that space is to keep waiting, or to speak.
    householder
    • In family decisions this week — a school for the kids, a job change, a money move — explicitly distinguish the 'burden' you can act on through karma-yoga from the deeper burden of forgetfulness in the home, and address the second by establishing or strengthening one daily moment (a verse, a prasāda offering, a kīrtana) that puts Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet at the center of the household.
    • Teach your children, by your own example and not by lecture, the difference between material compassion (rescuing them from every discomfort) and real karuṇā (giving them a life oriented toward Kṛṣṇa) — pick one situation this week where you have been over-cushioning them out of bodily affection, and choose the harder, soul-serving response.
    • When you next walk into your office or workplace, train yourself to look for the marks of Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet there — in an honest colleague, in an unexpected mercy, in a problem solved beyond your effort — and at the end of the day, name them in svādhyāya before bed; this slowly converts a 'workplace' into a place where you remember the Lord.
    senior
    • You have already 'transitioned through' more bodies than the youth in your family can imagine — use this season to speak less about your past achievements and more, when asked, about the lotus feet that have actually carried you; mentoring in the Gauḍīya line is not transferring your story, it is pointing past yourself to Kṛṣṇa.
    • Loosen one specific attachment this month — a possession, a role, a grievance you have been polishing for decades — and offer the loosening at His lotus feet, not as renunciation for its own sake, but to make room in your consciousness for the kind of absorption Prabhupāda describes the gopīs and Vṛndāvana Vaiṣṇavas as having twenty-four hours a day.
    • When mortality crosses your mind — a friend's diagnosis, your own body's signals — do not swerve away into distraction or into impersonal consolations about 'energy' or 'the universe'; instead, return deliberately to thinking of Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, knowing from this verse that one who is so absorbed na bhavāya kalpate — is not made for further material existence.
    Common Pitfalls
    • Treating tavānukampitām (His causeless mercy) as something to be earned by sādhana, rather than received humbly — turning devotional practice into a transaction and then resenting Kṛṣṇa when the 'vision' does not arrive on schedule.
    • Romanticizing Vṛndāvana-dhāma as a tourist destination — believing that physically traveling there substitutes for the inner cultivation of always hearing, chanting, and thinking of His lotus feet wherever one currently lives.
    • Conflating relief from material burdens (the demons being killed) with spiritual advancement — celebrating when life's difficulties ease and assuming that ease itself is Kṛṣṇa's mercy, rather than recognizing that real mercy is the awakened capacity to see His marks.
    Discussion Prompts
    • The demigods rejoice that the earth's burden is being removed by Kṛṣṇa's appearance. Where in your own life do you secretly hope someone (or something) else removes a burden you've been quietly enabling — and what would it mean to recognize Kṛṣṇa, not circumstance, as the one who actually relieves it?
    • Akrūra fell down groaning when he saw the marks of Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet on Vṛndāvana's soil. Most of us would walk over the same ground and notice nothing. Share with your partner one concrete habit of perception you would need to change to even begin to see śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-padma in the world around you — and where you suspect you are unwilling to make that change.
    • Prabhupāda says the gopīs were 'beyond the material platform' simply by thinking of the Lord's lotus feet. A skeptic in the room would say this is escapism dressed up as spirituality. How would you distinguish absorption in Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet from a sophisticated form of avoidance — and have you ever blurred the two in your own sādhana?
    Role Play

    A small group is leading a Sunday class for newcomers. One newcomer raises her hand: 'I love the idea that Kṛṣṇa walked the earth and left footprints, but honestly, when I went to Vṛndāvana last year I just saw dust, monkeys, and souvenir shops. I felt nothing. Am I doing something wrong, or is this whole tavānukampitām thing reserved for people the Lord has already favored — which feels like a closed loop?' Two students play the facilitators. One must respond from the verse and purport without retreating into platitudes ('keep chanting, it will come'); the other must press back as the newcomer until a real answer about causeless mercy, qualification, and the role of hearing/chanting/remembering the lotus feet is articulated. The teacher pauses the role-play whenever either side drifts into impersonalism or modern self-help.

    Objections & Responses
    • Talking about 'the burden of demons being removed by the Lord's appearance' sounds like mythological wish-fulfillment. In the actual world, evil people are removed by courts, armies, and political work — not by waiting for an avatāra. Isn't this verse just a pre-modern way of outsourcing responsibility?
      The demigods in this verse are not sitting back waiting — they are the very administrators of the universe, fully engaged in their duties. Their joy is not that they no longer have to act, but that the deepest burden — one that no court, army, or policy can finally lift — is being addressed at its root by Kṛṣṇa Himself. Material arrangements relieve symptoms; the burden the demigods name is the burden of asuric consciousness, of forgetfulness of Kṛṣṇa, which reproduces itself faster than any institution can contain it. A Gauḍīya practitioner does both: discharges sva-dharma in the world with full effort, and simultaneously recognizes that lasting relief comes only when Kṛṣṇa's presence is admitted into the field. That is not outsourcing; it is correctly locating the cause.
    • The purport says these footprint-marks are 'visible to devotees who receive the causeless mercy.' That is a perfectly unfalsifiable claim — the people who see the marks are the ones the Lord has favored, and the ones who do not are simply not favored yet. How is this different from any other in-group epistemology that protects itself from challenge?
      The criticism would land if Gauḍīya tradition told the unconvinced to wait passively for mercy to descend. It does not. Prabhupāda ends the purport with a precise, testable instruction: hear, chant, and think about the Lord's lotus feet, as the Vaiṣṇavas of Vṛndāvana do. The 'causeless' in causeless mercy means it is not earned as wages — but it is invited, and the invitation has a concrete form: śravaṇaṁ kīrtanaṁ smaraṇam. Anyone, of any background, can take up that practice today and check, over months and years, whether their perception of the world begins to change — whether dust starts to look like dust marked by Kṛṣṇa's feet. That is not a closed loop; it is an open door with a threshold that requires you to actually walk through it.
